अ॒न्तरि॑च्छन्ति॒ तं जने॑ रु॒द्रं प॒रो म॑नी॒षया॑
antár ichanti táṃ jáne rudrám paró manīṣáyā
Him, glowing bright beyond all thought, they seek among the race of man; With him for tougue they seize the food.
jāmy àtītape dhánur vayodhā́ aruhad vánam
He hath inflamed the twofold plain: lifegiving, he hath climbed the wood, And with his tongue hath struck the rock.
cáran vatsó rúśann ihá nidātā́raṃ ná vindate
Wandering here the radiant Calf finds none to fetter him, and seeks The Mother to declare his praise.
utó nv àsya yán mahád áśvāvad yójanam bṛhád
And now that great and mighty team, the team of horses that are his, And traces of his car, are seen.
duhánti saptaíkām úpa dvā́ páñca sṛjataḥ
The seven milk a single cow; the two set other five to work, On the stream's loud-resounding bank.
ā́ daśábhir vivásvata índraḥ kóśam acucyavīt
Entreated by Vivasvan's ten, Indra cast down the water-jar With threefold hammer from the sky.
pári tridhā́tur adhvaráṃ jūrṇír eti návīyasī
Three times the newly-kindled flame proceeds around the sacrifice: The priests anoint it with the meath.
With reverence they drain the fount that circles with its wheel above, Exhaustless, with the mouth below.
abhyā́ram íd ádrayo níṣiktam púṣkare mádhu
The pressing-stones are set at work: the meath is poured into the tank, At the out-shedding of the fount.
Ye cows, protect the fount: the two Mighty Ones bless the sacrifice. The handles twain are wrought of gold.
ā́ suté siñcata śríyaṃ ródasyor abhiśríyam
Pour on the juice the ornament which reaches both the heaven and earth Supply the liquid to the Bull.
ते जा॑नत॒ स्वमो॒क्यं१॒॑ सं व॒त्सासो॒ न मा॒तृभिः॑
té jānata svám okyàṃ sáṃ vatsā́so ná mātṛ́bhiḥ
These know their own abiding-place: like calves beside the mother cows They meet together with their kin.
उप॒ स्रक्वे॑षु॒ बप्स॑तः कृण्व॒ते ध॒रुणं॑ दि॒वि
úpa srákveṣu bápsataḥ kṛṇvaté dharúṇaṃ diví
Devouring in their greedy jaws, they make sustaining food in heaven, To Indra, Agni light and prayer.
ádhukṣat pipyúṣīm íṣam ū́rjaṃ saptápadīm aríḥ
The Pious One milked out rich food, sustenance dealt in portions seven, Together with the Sun's seven rays.
I took some Soma when the Sun rose up, O Mitra, Varuṇa. That is the sick man's medicine.
utó nv àsya yát padáṃ haryatásya nidhānyàm
From where oblations must be laid, which is the Well-beloved's home, He with his tongue hath compassed heaven.
73: úd īrāthām ṛtāyaté yuñjā́thām aśvinā rátham
ROUSE ye for him who keeps the Law, yoke your steeds, Aṣvins, to your car Let your protecting help be near.
nimíṣaś cij jávīyasā ráthenā́ yātam aśvinā
Come, Aṣvins, with your car more swift than is the twinkling of an eye Let your protecting help be near.
úpa stṛṇītam átraye hiména gharmám aśvinā
Aṣvins, ye overlaid with cold the fiery pit for Atri's sake: Let your protecting help be near.
कुह॑ स्थः॒ कुह॑ जग्मथुः॒ कुह॑ श्ये॒नेव॑ पेतथुः
kúha sthaḥ kúha jagmathuḥ kúha śyenéva petathuḥ
Where are ye? whither are ye gone? whither, like falcons, have ye flown? Let your protecting help be near.
yád adyá kárhi kárhi cic chuśrūyā́tam imáṃ hávam
If ye at any time this day are listening to this my call, Let your protecting help be near.
The Aṣvins, fust to hear our prayer, for closest kinship I approach: Let your protecting help be near.
ávantam átraye gṛháṃ kṛṇutáṃ yuvám aśvinā
For Atri ye, O Aṣvins, made a dwellingplace to shield him well, Let your protecting help be near.
várethe agním ātápo vádate valgv átraye
Ye warded off the fervent heat for Atri when he sweetly spake: Let your protecting help be near.
prá saptávadhrir āśásā dhā́rām agnér aśāyata
Erst Saptavadbri by his prayer obtained the trenchant edge of fire: Let your protecting help be near.
इ॒हा ग॑तं वृषण्वसू शृणु॒तं म॑ इ॒मं हव॑म्
ihā́ gataṃ vṛṣaṇvasū śṛṇutám ma imáṃ hávam
Come hither, O ye Lords of wealth, and listen to this call of mine: Let your protecting help be near.
kím idáṃ vām purāṇaváj járator iva śasyate
What is this praise told forth of you as Elders in the ancient way? Let your protecting help be near.
samānáṃ vāṃ sajātyàṃ samānó bándhur aśvinā
One common brotherhood is yours, Aṣvins your kindred is the same: Let your protecting help be near.
यो वां॒ रजां॑स्यश्विना॒ रथो॑ वि॒याति॒ रोद॑सी
yó vāṃ rájāṃsy aśvinā rátho viyā́ti ródasī
This is your chariot, Aṣvins, which speeds through the regions, earth and heaven: Let your protecting aid be near.
ā́ no gávyebhir áśvyaiḥ sahásrair úpa gachatam
Approach ye hitherward to us with thousands both of steeds and kine : Let your protecting help be near.
mā́ no gávyebhir áśvyaiḥ sahásrebhir áti khyatam
Pass us not by, remember us with thousands both of kine and steeds; Let your protecting help be near.
aruṇápsur uṣā́ abhūd ákar jyótir ṛtā́varī
The purple tinted Dawn hath risen, and true to Law hath made the light: Let your protecting help be near.
aśvínā sú vicā́kaśad vṛkṣám paraśumā́m̐ iva
He looked upon the Aṣvins, as an axe-armed man upon a tree: Let your protecting help be near.
पुरं॒ न धृ॑ष्ण॒वा रु॑ज कृ॒ष्णया॑ बाधि॒तो वि॒शा
púraṃ ná dhṛṣṇav ā́ ruja kṛṣṇáyā bādhitó viśā́
By the black band encompassed round, break it down, bold one, like a fort. Let your protecting help be near.
74: अ॒ग्निं वो॒ दुर्यं॒ वचः॑ स्तु॒षे शू॒षस्य॒ मन्म॑भिः
agníṃ vo dúryaṃ váca stuṣé śūṣásya mánmabhiḥ
EXERTING all our strength with thoughts of power we glorify in speech Agni your dear familiar Friend, the darling Guest in every home.
यं जना॑सो ह॒विष्म॑न्तो मि॒त्रं न स॒र्पिरा॑सुतिम्
yáṃ jánāso havíṣmanto mitráṃ ná sarpírāsutim
Whom, served with sacrificial oil like Mitra, men presenting gifts Eulogize with their songs of praise
Much-lauded Jâtavedas, him who bears oblations up to heaven Prepared in service of the Gods.
yásya śrutárvā bṛhánn ārkṣó ánīka édhate
To noblest Agni, Friend of man, best Vr̥itra-slayer, are we come, Him in whose presenceR̥iksha's son, mighty Ṣrutarvan, waxes great;
To deathless Jâtavedas, meet for praise, adored, with sacred oil, Visible through the gloom of night
sabā́dho yáṃ jánā imè 'gníṃ havyébhir ī́ḷate
Even Agni whom these priestly men worship with sacrificial gifts, With lifted ladles offering them.
iyáṃ te návyasī matír ágne ádhāyy asmád ā́
O Agni, this our newest hymn hath been addressed from us to thee, O cheerful Guest, well-born, most wise, worker of wonders, ne'er deceived.
सा ते॑ अग्ने॒ शंत॑मा॒ चनि॑ष्ठा भवतु प्रि॒या
sā́ te agne śáṃtamā cániṣṭhā bhavatu priyā́
Agni, may it be dear to thee, most grateful, and exceeding sweet: Grow mightier, eulogized therewith.
sā́ dyumnaír dyumnínī bṛhád úpopa śrávasi śrávaḥ
Splendid with splendours may it be, and in the battle with the foe Add loftier glory to thy fame.
यस्य॒ श्रवां॑सि॒ तूर्व॑थ॒ पन्य॑म्पन्यं च कृ॒ष्टयः॑
áśvam íd gā́ṃ rathaprā́ṃ tveṣám índraṃ ná sátpatim
yásya śrávāṃsi tū́rvatha pányam-panyaṃ ca kṛṣṭáyaḥ
Steed, cow, a lord of heroes, bright like Indra, who shall fill the car. Whose high renown ye celebrate, and people praise each glorious deed.
यं त्वा॑ गो॒पव॑नो गि॒रा चनि॑ष्ठदग्ने अङ्गिरः
yáṃ tvā gopávano girā́ cániṣṭhad agne aṅgiraḥ
Thou whom Gopavana made glad with song, O Agni Angiras, Hear this my call, thou Holy One.
यं त्वा॒ जना॑स॒ ईळ॑ते स॒बाधो॒ वाज॑सातये
yáṃ tvā jánāsa ī́ḷate sabā́dho vā́jasātaye
Thou whom the priestly folk implore to aid the gathering of the spoil, Such be thou in the fight with foes.
I, called to him who reels with joy, Ṣrutarvan, Riksha’s son, shall stroke The heads of four presented steeds, like the long wool of fleecy rams.
सु॒रथा॑सो अ॒भि प्रयो॒ वक्ष॒न्वयो॒ न तुग्र्य॑म्
suráthāso abhí práyo vákṣan váyo ná túgryam
Four coursers with a splendid car, Savistha’s horses, fleet of foot, Shall bring me to the sacred feast, as flying steeds brought Tugra’s son.
satyám ít tvā mahenadi páruṣṇy áva dediśam
ném āpo aśvadā́taraḥ śáviṣṭhād asti mártyaḥ
The very truth do I declare to thee, Parushṇî, mighty flood. Waters! no man is there who gives more horses than Savishtha gives.
75: यु॒क्ष्वा हि दे॑व॒हूत॑माँ॒ अश्वाँ॑ अग्ने र॒थीरि॑व
yukṣvā́ hí devahū́tamām̐ áśvām̐ agne rathī́r iva
YOKE, Agni, as a charioteer, thy steeds who best invite the Gods: As ancient Herald seat thyself.
उ॒त नो॑ देव दे॒वाँ अच्छा॑ वोचो वि॒दुष्ट॑रः
utá no deva devā́m̐ áchā voco vidúṣṭaraḥ
And, God, as skilfullest of all, call for us hitherward the Gods: Give all our wishes sure effect.
tváṃ ha yád yaviṣṭhya sáhasaḥ sūnav āhuta
For thou, Most Youthful, Son of Strength, thou to whom sacrifice is paid, Art holy, faithful to the Law.
ayám agníḥ sahasríṇo vā́jasya śatínas pátiḥ
This Agni, Lord of wealth and spoil hundredfold, thousandfold, is head And chief of riches and a Sage.
táṃ nemím ṛbhávo yathā́ namasva sáhūtibhiḥ
As craftsmen bend the felly, so bend at our general call: come nigh, Angiras, to the sacrifice.
tásmai nūnám abhídyave vācā́ virūpa nítyayā
Now, O Virûpa, rouse for him, Strong God who shines at early morn, Fair praise with voice that ceases not.
kám u ṣvid asya sénayāgnér ápākacakṣasaḥ
With missile of this Agni, his who looks afar, will we lay low The thief in combat for the kine.
mā́ no devā́nāṃ víśaḥ prasnātī́r ivosrā́ḥ
Let not the Companies of Gods fail us, like Dawns that float away, Like cows who leave the niggardly.
मा नः॑ समस्य दू॒ढ्य१॒॑ः परि॑द्वेषसो अंह॒तिः
mā́ naḥ samasya dūḍhyàḥ páridveṣaso aṃhatíḥ
Let not the sinful tyranny of any fiercely hating foe Smite us, as billows smite a ship.
नम॑स्ते अग्न॒ ओज॑से गृ॒णन्ति॑ देव कृ॒ष्टयः॑
námas te agna ójase gṛṇánti deva kṛṣṭáyaḥ
O Agni, God, the people sing reverent praise to thee for strength: With terrors trouble thou the foe.
kuvít sú no gáviṣṭayé 'gne saṃvéṣiṣo rayím
Wilt thou not, Agni, lend us aid in winning cattle, winning wealth? Maker of room, make room for us.
mā́ no asmín mahādhané párā varg bhārabhṛ́d yathā
In this great battle cast us not aside as one who bears a load: Snatch up the wealih and win it all.
anyám asmád bhiyā́ iyám ágne síṣaktu duchúnā
O Agni, let this plague pursue and fright another and not us: Make our impetuous strength more strong.
The reverent or unwearied man whose holy labour he accepts, Him Agni favours with success.
párasyā ádhi saṃvátó 'varām̐ abhy ā́ tara
Abandoning the foeman’s host pass hither to this company: Assist the men with whom I stand.
वि॒द्मा हि ते॑ पु॒रा व॒यमग्ने॑ पि॒तुर्यथाव॑सः
vidmā́ hí te purā́ vayám ágne pitúr yáthā́vasaḥ
As we have known thy gracious help, as of a Father, long agi, So now we pray to thee for bliss.
76: imáṃ nú māyínaṃ huva índram ī́śānam ójasā
NOT to forsake me, I invoke this Indra girt by Maruts, Lord Of magic power who rules with might.
ayám índro marútsakhā ví vṛtrásyābhinac chíraḥ
This Indra with his Marut Friends clave into pieces Vritra's head With hundred-knotted thunderbolt.
Indra, with Marut Friends grown strong, hath rent asunder Vritra, and Released the waters of the sea.
अ॒यं ह॒ येन॒ वा इ॒दं स्व॑र्म॒रुत्व॑ता जि॒तम्
ayáṃ ha yéna vā́ idáṃ svàr marútvatā jitám
This is that Indra who, begirt by Maruts, won the light of heaven That he might drink the Soma juice.
Mighty, impetuous, begirt by Maruts, him who loudly roars, Indra we invocate with songs.
Indra begirt by Maruts we invoke after the ancient plan, That he may drink the Soma juice.
म॒रुत्वाँ॑ इन्द्र मीढ्वः॒ पिबा॒ सोमं॑ शतक्रतो
marútvām̐ indra mīḍhvaḥ píbā sómaṃ śatakrato
O liberal Indra, Marut-girt, much-lauded Ṣatakratu, drink The Soma at this sacrifice.
túbhyéd indra marútvate sutā́ḥ sómāso adrivaḥ
To thee, O Indra, Marut-girt, these Soma juices, Thunderer! Are offered from the heart with lauds.
píbéd indra marútsakhā sutáṃ sómaṃ díviṣṭiṣu
Drink, Indra, with thy Marut Friends, pressed Soma at the morning rites, Whetting thy thunderbolt with strength.
uttíṣṭhann ójasā sahá pītvī́ śípre avepayaḥ
Arising in thy might, thy jaws thou shookest, Indra, having quaffed The Soma which the mortar pressed.
ánu tvā ródasī ubhé krákṣamāṇam akṛpetām
Indra, both worlds complained to thee when uttering thy fearful roar, What time thou smotest Dasyus dead.
From Indra have I measured out a song eight-footed with nine parts, Delicate, faithful to the Law.
77: jajñānó nú śatákratur ví pṛchad íti mātáram
SCARCELY was Ṣatakratu, born when of his Mother he inquired, Who are the mighty? Who are famed?
ā́d īṃ śavasy àbravīd aurṇavābhám ahīśúvam
Then Ṣavasî declared to him Aurṇavâbha, Ahîṣuva: Son, these be they thou must o'erthrow
sám ít tā́n vṛtrahā́khidat khé arā́m̐ iva khédayā
The Vritra-slayer smote them all as spokes are hammered into naves: The Dasyu-killer waxed in might.
Then Indra at a single draught drank the contents of thirty pails, Pails that were filled with Soma juice.
abhí gandharvám atṛṇad abudhnéṣu rájassv ā́
Indra in groundless realms of space pierced the Gandharva through, that he Might make Brahmans' strength increase.
nír āvidhyad giríbhya ā́ dhāráyat pakvám odanám
Down from the mountains Indra shot hither his well-directed shaft: He gained the ready brew of rice.
śatábradhna íṣus táva sahásraparṇa éka ít
One only is that shaft of thine, with thousand feathers, hundred barbs, Which, Indra, thou hast made thy friend.
तेन॑ स्तो॒तृभ्य॒ आ भ॑र॒ नृभ्यो॒ नारि॑भ्यो॒ अत्त॑वे
téna stotṛ́bhya ā́ bhara nṛ́bhyo nā́ribhyo áttave
Strong as the Ribhus at thy birth, therewith to those who praise thee, men, And women, bring thou food to eat.
ए॒ता च्यौ॒त्नानि॑ ते कृ॒ता वर्षि॑ष्ठानि॒ परी॑णसा
etā́ cyautnā́ni te kṛtā́ várṣiṣṭhāni párīṇasā
By thee these exploits were achieved, the mightiest deeds, abundantly: Firm in thy heart thou settest them.
víśvét tā́ víṣṇur ā́bharad urukramás tvéṣitaḥ
śatám mahiṣā́n kṣīrapākám odanáṃ varāhám índra emuṣám
All these things Vishṇu brought, the Lord of ample stride whom thou hadst sent- A hundred buffaloes, a brew of rice and milk: and Indra, slew the ravening boar
तु॒वि॒क्षं ते॒ सुकृ॑तं सू॒मयं॒ धनुः॑ सा॒धुर्बु॒न्दो हि॑र॒ण्ययः॑
उ॒भा ते॑ बा॒हू रण्या॒ सुसं॑स्कृत ऋदू॒पे चि॑दृदू॒वृधा॑
tuvikṣáṃ te súkṛtaṃ sūmáyaṃ dhánuḥ sādhúr bundó hiraṇyáyaḥ
ubhā́ te bāhū́ ráṇyā súsaṃskṛta ṛdūpé cid ṛdūvṛ́dhā
Most deadly is thy bow, successful, fashioned well: good is thine arrow, decked with gold. Warlike and well equipped thine arms are, which increase sweetness for him who drinks the sweet.
78: पु॒रो॒ळाशं॑ नो॒ अन्ध॑स॒ इन्द्र॑ स॒हस्र॒मा भ॑र
puroḷā́śaṃ no ándhasa índra sahásram ā́ bhara
BRING us a thousand, Indra, as our guerdon for the Soma juice: Hundreds of kine, O Hero, bring.
ā́ no bhara vyáñjanaṃ gā́m áśvam abhyáñjanam
Bring cattle, bring us ornament, bring us embellishment and steeds, Give us, besides, two rings of gold.
उ॒त नः॑ कर्ण॒शोभ॑ना पु॒रूणि॑ धृष्ण॒वा भ॑र
utá naḥ karṇaśóbhanā purū́ṇi dhṛṣṇav ā́ bhara
And, Bold One, bring in ample store rich jewels to adorn the ear, For thou, Good Lord, art far renowned.
नकीं॑ वृधी॒क इ॑न्द्र ते॒ न सु॒षा न सु॒दा उ॒त
nákīṃ vṛdhīká indra te ná suṣā́ ná sudā́ utá
None other is there for the priest, Hero! but thou, to give him gifts, To win much spoil and prosper him.
nákīm índro níkartave ná śakráḥ páriśaktave
Indra can never be brought low, Ṣakra can never be subdued: He heareth and beholdeth all.
sá manyúm mártyānām ádabdho ní cikīṣate
He spieth out the wrath of man, he who can never be deceived: Ere blame can come he marketh it.
krátva ít pūrṇám udáraṃ turásyāsti vidhatáḥ
He hath his stomach full of might, the Vritra-slayer, Conqueror, The Soma-drinker, ordering all.
त्वे वसू॑नि॒ संग॑ता॒ विश्वा॑ च सोम॒ सौभ॑गा
tvé vásūni sáṃgatā víśvā ca soma saúbhagā
In thee all treasures are combined, Soma all blessed things in thee, Uninjured, easy to bestow.
tvā́m íd yavayúr máma kā́mo gavyúr hiraṇyayúḥ
To thee speeds forth my hope that craves the gift of corn, and kine and gold, Yea, craving horses, speeds to thee.
दि॒नस्य॑ वा मघव॒न्त्सम्भृ॑तस्य वा पू॒र्धि यव॑स्य का॒शिना॑
távéd indrāhám āśásā háste dā́traṃ canā́ dade
dinásya vā maghavan sámbhṛtasya vā pūrdhí yávasya kāśínā
Indra, through hope in thee alone even this sickle do I grasp. Fill my hand, Maghavan, with all that it can hold of barley cut or gathered up.
79: ayáṃ kṛtnúr ágṛbhīto viśvajíd udbhíd ít sómaḥ
THIS here is Soma, ne'er restrained, active, all-conquering bursting forth, Rishi and Sage by sapience,
abhy ūā̀rṇoti yán nagnám bhiṣákti víśvaṃ yát turám
prém andháḥ khyan níḥ śroṇó bhūt
All that is bare he covers o'er, all that is sick he medicines; The blind man sees, the cripple walks.
Thou, Soma, givest wide defence against the hate of alien men, Hatreds that waste and weaken us.
त्वं चि॒त्ती तव॒ दक्षै॑र्दि॒व आ पृ॑थि॒व्या ऋ॑जीषिन्
tváṃ cittī́ táva dákṣair divá ā́ pṛthivyā́ ṛjīṣin
Thou by thine insight and thy skill, Impetuous One, from heaven and earth Drivest the sinner's enmity.
arthíno yánti céd árthaṃ gáchān íd dadúṣo rātím
When to their task they come with zeal, may they obtain the Giver's grace, And satisfy his wish who thirsts.
vidád yát pūrvyáṃ naṣṭám úd īm ṛtāyúm īrayat
So may he find what erst was lost, so may be speed the pious man, And lengthen his remaining life.
Gracious, displaying tender love, unconquered, gentle in thy thoughts, Be sweet, O Soma, to our heart.
मा नः॑ सोम॒ सं वी॑विजो॒ मा वि बी॑भिषथा राजन्
mā́ naḥ soma sáṃ vīvijo mā́ ví bībhiṣathā rājan
O Soma, terrify us not; strike us not with alarm, O King: Wound not our heart with dazzling flame.
राज॒न्नप॒ द्विषः॑ सेध॒ मीढ्वो॒ अप॒ स्रिधः॑ सेध
áva yát své sadhásthe devā́nāṃ durmatī́r ī́kṣe
rā́jann ápa dvíṣaḥ sedha mī́ḍhvo ápa srídhaḥ sedha
When in my dwelling-place I see the wicked enemies of Gods, King, chase their hatred far away, thou Bounteous One, dispel our foes.
80: O Ṣatakratu! truly I have made none else my Comforter. Indra; be gracious unto us.
Thou who hast ever aided us kindly of old to win the spoil, As such, O Indra, favour us.
What now? As prompter of the poor thou helpest him who sheds the juice. Wilt thou not, Indra, strengthen us?
índra prá ṇo rátham ava paścā́c cit sántam adrivaḥ
O Indra, help our chariot on, yea, Thunderer, though it lag behind: Give this my car the foremost place.
हन्तो॒ नु किमा॑ससे प्रथ॒मं नो॒ रथं॑ कृधि
hánto nú kím āsase prathamáṃ no ráthaṃ kṛdhi
Ho there! why sittest thou at case? Make thou my chariot to be first And bring the fame of victory near.
अवा॑ नो वाज॒युं रथं॑ सु॒करं॑ ते॒ किमित्परि॑
ávā no vājayúṃ ráthaṃ sukáraṃ te kím ít pári
Assist our car that seeks the prize. What can be easier for thee? So make thou us victorious.
इन्द्र॒ दृह्य॑स्व॒ पूर॑सि भ॒द्रा त॑ एति निष्कृ॒तम्
índra dṛ́hyasva pū́r asi bhadrā́ ta eti niṣkṛtám
Indra, be firm: a fort art thou. To thine appointed place proceeds The auspicious hymn in season due.
मा सी॑मव॒द्य आ भा॑गु॒र्वी काष्ठा॑ हि॒तं धन॑म्
mā́ sīm avadyá ā́ bhāg urvī́ kā́ṣṭhā hitáṃ dhánam
Let not our portion be disgrace. Broad is the course, the prize is set, The barriers are opened wide.
turī́yaṃ nā́ma yajñíyaṃ yadā́ káras tád uśmasi
This thing we wish. that thou mayst take thy fourth, thy sacrificial name. So art thou held to be our Lord.
अवी॑वृधद्वो अमृता॒ अम॑न्दीदेक॒द्यूर्दे॑वा उ॒त याश्च॑ देवीः
तस्मा॑ उ॒ राधः॑ कृणुत प्रश॒स्तं प्रा॒तर्म॒क्षू धि॒याव॑सुर्जगम्यात्
ávīvṛdhad vo amṛtā ámandīd ekadyū́r devā utá yā́ś ca devīḥ
tásmā u rā́dhaḥ kṛṇuta praśastám prātár makṣū́ dhiyā́vasur jagamyāt
Ekadyû hath exalted you, Immortals: both Goddesses and Gods hath he delighted. Bestow upon him bounty meet for praises. May he, enriched with prayer, come soon and early.
81: आ तू न॑ इन्द्र क्षु॒मन्तं॑ चि॒त्रं ग्रा॒भं सं गृ॑भाय
ā́ tū́ na indra kṣumántaṃ citráṃ grābháṃ sáṃ gṛbhāya
INDRA, God of the mighty arm, gather for us with thy right hand Manifold and nutritious spoil.
वि॒द्मा हि त्वा॑ तुविकू॒र्मिं तु॒विदे॑ष्णं तु॒वीम॑घम्
vidmā́ hí tvā tuvikūrmíṃ tuvídeṣṇaṃ tuvī́magham
We know thee mighty in thy deeds, of mighty bounty, mighty wealth, Mighty in measure, prompt to aid.
न॒हि त्वा॑ शूर दे॒वा न मर्ता॑सो॒ दित्स॑न्तम्
nahí tvā śūra devā́ ná mártāso dítsantam
Hero, when thou art fain to give, neither may Gods nor mortal men Restrain thee like a fearful Bull.
éto nv índraṃ stávāméśānaṃ vásvaḥ svarā́jam
Come, let us glorify Indra, Lord supreme of wealth, Self-ruling King: In bounty may he harm us not.
prá stoṣad úpa gāsiṣac chrávat sā́ma gīyámānam
Let prelude sound and following chant so let him hear the Sâman sung, And with his bounty answer us.
आ नो॑ भर॒ दक्षि॑णेना॒भि स॒व्येन॒ प्र मृ॑श
ā́ no bhara dákṣiṇenābhí savyéna prá mṛśa
índra mā́ no vásor nír bhāk
O Indra, with thy right hand bring, and with thy left remember us. Let us not lose our share of wealth.
उप॑ क्रम॒स्वा भ॑र धृष॒ता धृ॑ष्णो॒ जना॑नाम्
úpa kramasvā́ bhara dhṛṣatā́ dhṛṣṇo jánānām
Come nigh, O Bold One, boldly bring hither the riches of the churl Who giveth least of all the folk.
इन्द्र॒ य उ॒ नु ते॒ अस्ति॒ वाजो॒ विप्रे॑भिः॒ सनि॑त्वः
índra yá u nú te ásti vā́jo víprebhiḥ sánitvaḥ
Indra, the booty which thou hast with holy singers to receive, Even that booty win with us.
Indra, thy swiftly-coming spoil, the booty which rejoices all, Sounds quick in concert with our hopes.
82: ā́ prá drava parāváto 'rvāvátaś ca vṛtrahan
HASTE forward to us from afar, or, Vritra-slayer, from anear, To meet the offering to the meath.
ती॒व्राः सोमा॑स॒ आ ग॑हि सु॒तासो॑ मादयि॒ष्णवः॑
tīvrā́ḥ sómāsa ā́ gahi sutā́so mādayiṣṇávaḥ
Strong are the Soma-draughts; come nigh: the juices fill thee with delight: Drink boldly even as thou art wont'.
iṣā́ mandasvā́d u té 'raṃ várāya manyáve
Joy, Indra, in the strengthening food: let it content thy wish and thought, And be delightful to thine heart.
आ त्व॑शत्र॒वा ग॑हि॒ न्यु१॒॑क्थानि॑ च हूयसे
ā́ tv àśatrav ā́ gahi ny ùkthā́ni ca hūyase
Come to us thou who hast no foe: we call thee down to hymns of praise, In heaven's sublimest realm of light.
तुभ्या॒यमद्रि॑भिः सु॒तो गोभिः॑ श्री॒तो मदा॑य॒ कम्
túbhyāyám ádribhiḥ sutó góbhiḥ śrītó mádāya kám
This Soma here expressed with stones and dressed with milk for thy carouse, Indra, is offered up to thee.
इन्द्र॑ श्रु॒धि सु मे॒ हव॑म॒स्मे सु॒तस्य॒ गोम॑तः
índra śrudhí sú me hávam asmé sutásya gómataḥ
Graciously, Indra, hear my call. Come and obtain the draught, and sate Thyself with juices blent with milk.
य इ॑न्द्र चम॒सेष्वा सोम॑श्च॒मूषु॑ ते सु॒तः
yá indra camaséṣv ā́ sómaś camū́ṣu te sutáḥ
The Soma, Indra, which is shed in chalices and vats for thee, Drink thou, for thou art Lord thereof.
यो अ॒प्सु च॒न्द्रमा॑ इव॒ सोम॑श्च॒मूषु॒ ददृ॑शे
yó apsú candrámā iva sómaś camū́ṣu dádṛśe
The Soma seen within the vats, as in the flood the Moon is seen, Drink thou, for thou art Lord thereof.
yáṃ te śyenáḥ padā́bharat tiró rájāṃsy áspṛtam
That which the Hawk brought in his claw, inviolate, through the air to thee, Drink thou, for thou art Lord thereof.
83: devā́nām íd ávo mahát tád ā́ vṛṇīmahe vayám
WE choose unto ourselves that high protection of the Mighty Gods That it may help and succour us.
ते नः॑ सन्तु॒ युजः॒ सदा॒ वरु॑णो मि॒त्रो अ॑र्य॒मा
té naḥ santu yújaḥ sádā váruṇo mitró aryamā́
May they be ever our allies, Varuṇa, Mitra, Aryaman, Far-seeing Gods who prosper us.
अति॑ नो विष्पि॒ता पु॒रु नौ॒भिर॒पो न प॑र्षथ
áti no viṣpitā́ purú naubhír apó ná parṣatha
Ye furtherers of holy Law, transport us safe o'er many woes, As over water-floods in ships.
vāmáṃ no astv aryaman vāmáṃ varuṇa śáṃsyam
Dear wealth be Aryaman to us, Varuṇa dear wealth meet for praise: Dear wealth we choose unto ourselves.
For Sovrans of dear wealth are ye, Âdityas, not of sinner's wealth, Ye sapient Gods who slay the foe.
vayám íd vaḥ sudānavaḥ kṣiyánto yā́nto ádhvann ā́
We in our homes, ye Bounteous Ones, and while we journey on the road, Invoke you, Gods, to prosper us.
Regard us, Indra, Vishṇu, here, ye Aṣvins and the Marut host, Us who are kith and kin to you.
Ye Bounteous Ones, from time of old we here set forth our brotherhood, Our kinship in the Mother's womb.
यू॒यं हि ष्ठा सु॑दानव॒ इन्द्र॑ज्येष्ठा अ॒भिद्य॑वः
yūyáṃ hí ṣṭhā́ sudānava índrajyeṣṭhā abhídyavaḥ
Then come with Indra for your chief, as early day, ye Bounteous Gods Yea, I address you now for this.
84: प्रेष्ठं॑ वो॒ अति॑थिं स्तु॒षे मि॒त्रमि॑व प्रि॒यम्
préṣṭhaṃ vo átithiṃ stuṣé mitrám iva priyám
AGNI, your dearest Guest, I laud, him who is loving as a friend, Who brings us riches like a car.
क॒विमि॑व॒ प्रचे॑तसं॒ यं दे॒वासो॒ अध॑ द्वि॒ता
kavím iva prácetasaṃ yáṃ devā́so ádha dvitā́
Whom as a far-foreseeing Sage the Gods have, from the olden time, Established among mortal men.
त्वं य॑विष्ठ दा॒शुषो॒ नॄँः पा॑हि शृणु॒धी गिरः॑
tváṃ yaviṣṭha dāśúṣo nṛṛ́m̐ḥ pāhi śṛṇudhī́ gíraḥ
Do thou, Most Youthful God, protect the men who offer, hear their songs, And of thyself preserve their seed.
कया॑ ते अग्ने अङ्गिर॒ ऊर्जो॑ नपा॒दुप॑स्तुतिम्
káyā te agne aṅgira ū́rjo napād úpastutim
What is the praise wherewith, O God, Afigiras, Agni, Son of Strength, We, after thine own wish and thought,
दाशे॑म॒ कस्य॒ मन॑सा य॒ज्ञस्य॑ सहसो यहो
dā́śema kásya mánasā yajñásya sahaso yaho
May serve thee, O thou Child of Power, and with what sacrifice's plan? What prayer shall I now speak to thee?
अधा॒ त्वं हि न॒स्करो॒ विश्वा॑ अ॒स्मभ्यं॑ सुक्षि॒तीः
ádhā tváṃ hí nas káro víśvā asmábhyaṃ sukṣitī́ḥ
Our God, make all of us to dwell in happy habitations, and Reward our songs with spoil and wealth.
कस्य॑ नू॒नं परी॑णसो॒ धियो॑ जिन्वसि दम्पते
kásya nūnám párīṇaso dhíyo jinvasi dampate
Lord of the house, what plenty fills the songs which thou inspirest now, Thou whose hymn helps to win the kine?
Him Wise and Strong they glorify, the foremost Champion in the fray, And mighty in his dwelling-place.
क्षेति॒ क्षेमे॑भिः सा॒धुभि॒र्नकि॒र्यं घ्नन्ति॒ हन्ति॒ यः
kṣéti kṣémebhiḥ sādhúbhir nákir yáṃ ghnánti hánti yáḥ
Agni, he dwells in rest and peace who smites and no one smites again: With hero sons he prospers well
85: आ मे॒ हवं॑ नास॒त्याश्वि॑ना॒ गच्छ॑तं यु॒वम्
ā́ me hávaṃ nāsatyā́śvinā gáchataṃ yuvám
To this mine invocation, O ye Aṣvins, ye Nâsatyas, come, To drink the savoury Soma juice.
इ॒मं मे॒ स्तोम॑मश्विने॒मं मे॑ शृणुतं॒ हव॑म्
imám me stómam aśvinemám me śṛṇutaṃ hávam
This laud of mine, ye Aṣvins Twain, and this mine invitation hear, To drink the savoury Soma juice.
अ॒यं वां॒ कृष्णो॑ अश्विना॒ हव॑ते वाजिनीवसू
ayáṃ vāṃ kṛ́ṣṇo aśvinā hávate vājinīvasū
Here Kr̥ishṇa is invoking you, O Aṣvins, Lords of ample wealth. To drink the savoury Soma juice.
śṛṇutáṃ jaritúr hávaṃ kṛ́ṣṇasya stuvató narā
List, Heroes, to the singer's call, the call of Kr̥ishṇa lauding you, To drink the savoury Soma juice.
chardír yantam ádābhyaṃ víprāya stuvaté narā
Chiefs, to the sage who sings your praise grant an inviolable home, To drink the savoury Soma juice.
gáchataṃ dāśúṣo gṛhám itthā́ stuvató aśvinā
Come to the worshipper's abode, Aṣvins, who here is lauding you, To drink the savoury Soma juice.
Yoke to the firmly jointed car the ass which draws you, Lords of wealth. To drink the savoury Soma juice.
Come hither, Aṣvins, on your car of triple form with triple seat, To drink the savoury Soma juice.
नू मे॒ गिरो॑ नास॒त्याश्वि॑ना॒ प्राव॑तं यु॒वम्
nū́ me gíro nāsatyā́śvinā prā́vataṃ yuvám
O Aṣvins, O Nâsatyas, now accept with favouring grace my songs, To drink the savoury Soma juice.
86: उ॒भा हि द॒स्रा भि॒षजा॑ मयो॒भुवो॒भा दक्ष॑स्य॒ वच॑सो बभू॒वथुः॑
ता वां॒ विश्व॑को हवते तनूकृ॒थे मा नो॒ वि यौ॑ष्टं स॒ख्या मु॒मोच॑तम्
ubhā́ hí dasrā́ bhiṣájā mayobhúvobhā́ dákṣasya vácaso babhūváthuḥ
tā́ vāṃ víśvako havate tanūkṛthé mā́ no ví yauṣṭaṃ sakhyā́ mumócatam

YE Twain are wondrous strong, well-skilled in arts that heal, both bringers of delight, ye both won Daksha's praise. Viṣvaka calls on you as such to save his life. Break ye not off our friendship, come and set me free.
क॒था नू॒नं वां॒ विम॑ना॒ उप॑ स्तवद्यु॒वं धियं॑ ददथु॒र्वस्य॑इष्टये
ता वां॒ विश्व॑को हवते तनूकृ॒थे मा नो॒ वि यौ॑ष्टं स॒ख्या मु॒मोच॑तम्
kathā́ nūnáṃ vāṃ vímanā úpa stavad yuváṃ dhíyaṃ dadathur vásya .iṣṭaye
tā́ vāṃ víśvako havate tanūkṛthé mā́ no ví yauṣṭaṃ sakhyā́ mumócatam

How shall he praise you now who is distraught in mind? Ye Twain give wisdom for the gain of what is good. Viṣvaka calls on you as such to save his life. Break ye not off our friendship, come and set me free.
यु॒वं हि ष्मा॑ पुरुभुजे॒ममे॑ध॒तुं वि॑ष्णा॒प्वे॑ द॒दथु॒र्वस्य॑इष्टये
ता वां॒ विश्व॑को हवते तनूकृ॒थे मा नो॒ वि यौ॑ष्टं स॒ख्या मु॒मोच॑तम्
yuváṃ hí ṣmā purubhujemám edhatúṃ viṣṇāpvè dadáthur vásya .iṣṭaye
tā́ vāṃ víśvako havate tanūkṛthé mā́ no ví yauṣṭaṃ sakhyā́ mumócatam

Already have ye Twain, possessors of great wealth, prospered Vishṇâpû thus for gain of what is good. Viṣvaka calls on you as such to save his life. Break ye not off our friendship, come and set me free.
उ॒त त्यं वी॒रं ध॑न॒सामृ॑जी॒षिणं॑ दू॒रे चि॒त्सन्त॒मव॑से हवामहे
यस्य॒ स्वादि॑ष्ठा सुम॒तिः पि॒तुर्य॑था॒ मा नो॒ वि यौ॑ष्टं स॒ख्या मु॒मोच॑तम्
utá tyáṃ vīráṃ dhanasā́m ṛjīṣíṇaṃ dūré cit sántam ávase havāmahe
yásya svā́diṣṭhā sumatíḥ pitúr yathā mā́ no ví yauṣṭaṃ sakhyā́ mumócatam

And that Impetuous Hero, winner of the spoil, though he is far away, we call to succour us, Whose gracious favour, like a father's, is most sweet. Break ye not off our friendship, come and set me free.
ऋ॒तेन॑ दे॒वः स॑वि॒ता श॑मायत ऋ॒तस्य॒ शृङ्ग॑मुर्वि॒या वि प॑प्रथे
ऋ॒तं सा॑साह॒ महि॑ चित्पृतन्य॒तो मा नो॒ वि यौ॑ष्टं स॒ख्या मु॒मोच॑तम्
ṛténa deváḥ savitā́ śamāyata ṛtásya śṛ́ṅgam urviyā́ ví paprathe
ṛtáṃ sāsāha máhi cit pṛtanyató mā́ no ví yauṣṭaṃ sakhyā́ mumócatam
About the holy Law toils Savitar the God the horn of holy Law hath he spread far and wide. The holy Law hath quelled even mighty men of war. Break ye not off our ftiendship, come and set me free.
87: द्यु॒म्नी वां॒ स्तोमो॑ अश्विना॒ क्रिवि॒र्न सेक॒ आ ग॑तम्
मध्वः॑ सु॒तस्य॒ स दि॒वि प्रि॒यो न॑रा पा॒तं गौ॒रावि॒वेरि॑णे
dyumnī́ vāṃ stómo aśvinā krívir ná séka ā́ gatam
mádhvaḥ sutásya sá diví priyó narā pātáṃ gaurā́v ivériṇe
SPLENDID, O Aṣvins, is your praise. Come fountain-like, to pour the stream. Of the sweet juice effused-dear is it, Chiefs, in heaven-drink like two wild bulls at a pool.
पिब॑तं घ॒र्मं मधु॑मन्तमश्वि॒ना ब॒र्हिः सी॑दतं नरा
ता म॑न्दसा॒ना मनु॑षो दुरो॒ण आ नि पा॑तं॒ वेद॑सा॒ वयः॑
píbataṃ gharmám mádhumantam aśvinā́ barhíḥ sīdataṃ narā
tā́ mandasānā́ mánuṣo duroṇá ā́ ní pātaṃ védasā váyaḥ
Drink the libation rich in sweets, O Aṣvins Twain: sit. Heroes, on the sacred grass. Do ye with joyful heart in the abode of man preserve his life by means of wealth.
ता व॒र्तिर्या॑त॒मुप॑ वृ॒क्तब॑र्हिषो॒ जुष्टं॑ य॒ज्ञं दिवि॑ष्टिषु
ā́ vāṃ víśvābhir ūtíbhiḥ priyámedhā ahūṣata
tā́ vartír yātam úpa vṛktábarhiṣo júṣṭaṃ yajñáṃ díviṣṭiṣu
The Priyamedhas bid you come with all the succours that are yours. Come to his house whose holy grass is trimmed, to dear sacrifice at the morning rites.
पिब॑तं॒ सोमं॒ मधु॑मन्तमश्वि॒ना ब॒र्हिः सी॑दतं सु॒मत्
ता वा॑वृधा॒ना उप॑ सुष्टु॒तिं दि॒वो ग॒न्तं गौ॒रावि॒वेरि॑णम्
píbataṃ sómam mádhumantam aśvinā́ barhíḥ sīdataṃ sumát
tā́ vāvṛdhānā́ úpa suṣṭutíṃ divó gantáṃ gaurā́v ivériṇam
Drink ye the Soma rich in meath, ye Aṣvins Twain: sit gladly on the sacred grass. So, waxen mighty, to our eulogy from heaven come ye as wild-bulls to the pool.
dásrā híraṇyavartanī śubhas patī pātáṃ sómam ṛtāvṛdhā
Come to us, O ye Aṣvins, now with steeds of many a varied hue, Ye Lords of splendour, wondrous, borne on paths of gold, drink Soma, ye who strengthen Law.
व॒यं हि वां॒ हवा॑महे विप॒न्यवो॒ विप्रा॑सो॒ वाज॑सातये
ता व॒ल्गू द॒स्रा पु॑रु॒दंस॑सा धि॒याश्वि॑ना श्रु॒ष्ट्या ग॑तम्
vayáṃ hí vāṃ hávāmahe vipanyávo víprāso vā́jasātaye
tā́ valgū́ dasrā́ purudáṃsasā dhiyā́śvinā śruṣṭy ā́ gatam
For we the priestly singers, fain tohymn your praise, invoke you for the gain of strength. So, wondrous, fair, and famed for great deeds come to us, through our hymn, Aṣvins, when ye hear.
88: अ॒भि व॒त्सं न स्वस॑रेषु धे॒नव॒ इन्द्रं॑ गी॒र्भिर्न॑वामहे
táṃ vo dasmám ṛtīṣáhaṃ vásor mandānám ándhasaḥ
abhí vatsáṃ ná svásareṣu dhenáva índraṃ gīrbhír navāmahe
As cows low to their calves in stalls, so with our songs we glorify This Indra, even your Wondrous God who checks attack, who joys in the delicious juice.
द्यु॒क्षं सु॒दानुं॒ तवि॑षीभि॒रावृ॑तं गि॒रिं न पु॑रु॒भोज॑सम्
क्षु॒मन्तं॒ वाजं॑ श॒तिनं॑ सह॒स्रिणं॑ म॒क्षू गोम॑न्तमीमहे
dyukṣáṃ sudā́nuṃ táviṣībhir ā́vṛtaṃ giríṃ ná purubhójasam
kṣumántaṃ vā́jaṃ śatínaṃ sahasríṇam makṣū́ gómantam īmahe
Celestial, bounteous Giver, girt about with might, rich, mountain-like, in precious things, Him swift we seek. for foodful booty rich in kine, brought hundredfold and thousandfold.
न त्वा॑ बृ॒हन्तो॒ अद्र॑यो॒ वर॑न्त इन्द्र वी॒ळवः॑
यद्दित्स॑सि स्तुव॒ते माव॑ते॒ वसु॒ नकि॒ष्टदा मि॑नाति ते
ná tvā bṛhánto ádrayo váranta indra vīḷávaḥ
yád dítsasi stuvaté mā́vate vásu nákiṣ ṭád ā́ mināti te
Indra, the strong and lofty hills are powerless to bar thy way. None stay that act of thine when thou wouldst fain give wealth to one like me who sings thy praise.
योद्धा॑सि॒ क्रत्वा॒ शव॑सो॒त दं॒सना॒ विश्वा॑ जा॒ताभि म॒ज्मना॑
आ त्वा॒यम॒र्क ऊ॒तये॑ ववर्तति॒ यं गोत॑मा॒ अजी॑जनन्
yóddhāsi krátvā śávasotá daṃsánā víśvā jātā́bhí majmánā
ā́ tvāyám arká ūtáye vavartati yáṃ gótamā ájījanan
A Warrior thou by strength, wisdom, and wondrous deed, in might excellest all that is. Hither may this our hymn attract thee to our help, the hymn which Gotamas have made.
प्र हि रि॑रि॒क्ष ओज॑सा दि॒वो अन्ते॑भ्य॒स्परि॑
न त्वा॑ विव्याच॒ रज॑ इन्द्र॒ पार्थि॑व॒मनु॑ स्व॒धां व॑वक्षिथ
prá hí ririkṣá ójasā divó ántebhyas pári
ná tvā vivyāca rája indra pā́rthivam ánu svadhā́ṃ vavakṣitha
For in thy might thou stretchest out beyond the boundaries of heaven. The earthly region, Indra, comprehends thee not. After thy Godhead hast thou waxed.
nákiḥ páriṣṭir maghavan maghásya te yád dāśúṣe daśasyási
asmā́kam bodhy ucáthasya coditā́ máṃhiṣṭho vā́jasātaye
When, Maghavan, thou honourest the worshipper, no one is there to stay thy wealth. Most liberal Giver thou, do thou inspire our song of praise, that we may win the spoil.
89: yéna jyótir ájanayann ṛtāvṛ́dho deváṃ devā́ya jā́gṛvi
To Indra sing the lofty hymn, Maruts that slays the Vr̥itras best. Whereby the Holy Ones created for the God the light divine that ever wakes.
दे॒वास्त॑ इन्द्र स॒ख्याय॑ येमिरे॒ बृह॑द्भानो॒ मरु॑द्गण
devā́s ta indra sakhyā́ya yemire bṛ́hadbhāno márudgaṇa
Indra who quells the curse blew curses far away, and then in splendour came to us. Indra, refulgent with thy Marut host! the Gods strove eagerly to win thy love.
प्र व॒ इन्द्रा॑य बृह॒ते मरु॑तो॒ ब्रह्मा॑र्चत
prá va índrāya bṛhaté máruto bráhmārcata
vṛtráṃ hanati vṛtrahā́ śatákratur vájreṇa śatáparvaṇā
Sing to your lofty Indra, sing, Maruts, a holy hymn of praise. Let Ṣatakratu, Vr̥itra-slayer, kill the foe with hundred-knotted thunderbolt.
अ॒भि प्र भ॑र धृष॒ता धृ॑षन्मनः॒ श्रव॑श्चित्ते असद्बृ॒हत्
अर्ष॒न्त्वापो॒ जव॑सा॒ वि मा॒तरो॒ हनो॑ वृ॒त्रं जया॒ स्वः॑
abhí prá bhara dhṛṣatā́ dhṛṣanmanaḥ śrávaś cit te asad bṛhát
árṣantv ā́po jávasā ví mātáro háno vṛtráṃ jáyā svàḥ
Aim and fetch boldly forth, O thou whose heart is bold: great glory will be thine thereby. In rapid torrent let the mother waters spread. Slay Vr̥itra, win the light of heaven.
tát pṛthivī́m aprathayas tád astabhnā utá dyā́m
When thou, unequalled Maghavan, wast born to smite the Vr̥itras dead, Thou spreadest out the spacious earth and didst support and prop the heavens.
तत्ते॑ य॒ज्ञो अ॑जायत॒ तद॒र्क उ॒त हस्कृ॑तिः
tát te yajñó ajāyata tád arká utá háskṛtiḥ
tád víśvam abhibhū́r asi yáj jātáṃ yác ca jántvam
There was the sacrifice produced for thee, the laud, and song of joy, Thou in thy might surpassest all, all that now is and yet shall be.
आ॒मासु॑ प॒क्वमैर॑य॒ आ सूर्यं॑ रोहयो दि॒वि
घ॒र्मं न साम॑न्तपता सुवृ॒क्तिभि॒र्जुष्टं॒ गिर्व॑णसे बृ॒हत्
āmā́su pakvám aíraya ā́ sū́ryaṃ rohayo diví
gharmáṃ ná sā́man tapatā suvṛktíbhir júṣṭaṃ gírvaṇase bṛhát
Raw kine thou filledst with ripe milk. Thou madest Sûrya rise to heaven. Heat him as milk is heated with pure Sâma hymns, great joy to him who loves the song.
90: आ नो॒ विश्वा॑सु॒ हव्य॒ इन्द्रः॑ स॒मत्सु॑ भूषतु
उप॒ ब्रह्मा॑णि॒ सव॑नानि वृत्र॒हा प॑रम॒ज्या ऋची॑षमः
ā́ no víśvāsu hávya índraḥ samátsu bhūṣatu
úpa bráhmāṇi sávanāni vṛtrahā́ paramajyā́ ṛ́cīṣamaḥ
MAY Indra, who in every fight must be invoked, be near to us. May the most mighty Vr̥itra-slayer, meet for praise, come to libations and to hymns.
त्वं दा॒ता प्र॑थ॒मो राध॑साम॒स्यसि॑ स॒त्य ई॑शान॒कृत्
तु॒वि॒द्यु॒म्नस्य॒ युज्या वृ॑णीमहे पु॒त्रस्य॒ शव॑सो म॒हः
tváṃ dātā́ prathamó rā́dhasām asy ási satyá īśānakṛ́t
tuvidyumnásya yújyā́ vṛṇīmahe putrásya śávaso maháḥ
Thou art the best of all in sending bounteous gifts, true art thou, lordly in thine act. We claim alliance with the very Glorious One, yea, with the Mighty Son of Strength.
ब्रह्मा॑ त इन्द्र गिर्वणः क्रि॒यन्ते॒ अन॑तिद्भुता
इ॒मा जु॑षस्व हर्यश्व॒ योज॒नेन्द्र॒ या ते॒ अम॑न्महि
bráhmā ta indra girvaṇaḥ kriyánte ánatidbhutā
imā́ juṣasva haryaśva yójanéndra yā́ te ámanmahi
Prayers unsurpassed are offered up to thee the Lover of the Song. Indra, Lord of Bay Steeds, accept these fitting hymns, hymns which we have thought out for thee.
त्वं हि स॒त्यो म॑घव॒न्नना॑नतो वृ॒त्रा भूरि॑ न्यृ॒ञ्जसे॑
स त्वं श॑विष्ठ वज्रहस्त दा॒शुषे॒ऽर्वाञ्चं॑ र॒यिमा कृ॑धि
tváṃ hí satyó maghavann ánānato vṛtrā́ bhū́ri nyṛñjáse
sá tváṃ śaviṣṭha vajrahasta dāśúṣe 'rvā́ñcaṃ rayím ā́ kṛdhi
For thou, O Maghavan, art truthful, ne'er subdued and bringest many a Vr̥itra low. As such, O Mightiest Lord, Wielder of Thunder, send wealth hither to the worshipper.
tvám indra yaśā́ asy ṛjīṣī́ śavasas pate
tváṃ vṛtrā́ṇi haṃsy apratī́ny éka íd ánuttā carṣaṇīdhṛ́tā
O Indra, thou art far-renowned, impetuous, O Lord of Strength. Alone thou slayest with the guardian of mankind resistless never-conquered foes.
तमु॑ त्वा नू॒नम॑सुर॒ प्रचे॑तसं॒ राधो॑ भा॒गमि॑वेमहे
म॒हीव॒ कृत्तिः॑ शर॒णा त॑ इन्द्र॒ प्र ते॑ सु॒म्ना नो॑ अश्नवन्
tám u tvā nūnám asura prácetasaṃ rā́dho bhāgám ivemahe
mahī́va kṛ́ttiḥ śaraṇā́ ta indra prá te sumnā́ no aśnavan
As such we seek thee now, O Asura, thee most wise, craving thy bounty as our share. Thy sheltering defence is like a mighty cloak. So may thy glories reach to us.
91: अस्तं॒ भर॑न्त्यब्रवी॒दिन्द्रा॑य सुनवै त्वा श॒क्राय॑ सुनवै त्वा
kanyāā̀ vā́r avāyatī́ sómam ápi srutā́vidat
ástam bháranty abravīd índrāya sunavai tvā śakrā́ya sunavai tvā
DOWN to the stream a maiden came, and found the Soma by the way. Bearing it to her home she said, For Indra will I press thee out, for Ṣakra will I press thee out.
अ॒सौ य एषि॑ वीर॒को गृ॒हंगृ॑हं वि॒चाक॑शद्
asaú yá éṣi vīrakó gṛháṃ-gṛhaṃ vicā́kaśad
imáṃ jámbhasutam piba dhānā́vantaṃ karambhíṇam apūpávantam ukthínam
Thou roaming yonder, little man, beholding every house in turn, Drink thou this Soma pressed with teeth, accompanied with grain and curds, with cake of meal and song of praise.
आ च॒न त्वा॑ चिकित्सा॒मोऽधि॑ च॒न त्वा॒ नेम॑सि
ā́ caná tvā cikitsāmó 'dhi caná tvā némasi
śánair iva śanakaír ivéndrāyendo pári srava
Fain would we learn to know thee well, nor yet can we attain to thee. Still slowly and in gradual drops, O Indu, unto Indra flow.
kuvíc chákat kuvít kárat kuvín no vásyasas kárat
Will he not help and work for us? Will he not make us wealthier? Shall we not, hostile to our lord, unite ourselves to Indra now?
इ॒मानि॒ त्रीणि॑ वि॒ष्टपा॒ तानी॑न्द्र॒ वि रो॑हय
imā́ni trī́ṇi viṣṭápā tā́nīndra ví rohaya
śíras tatásyorvárām ā́d idám ma úpodáre
O Indra, cause to sprout again three places, these which I declare,– My father's head, his cultured field, and this the part below my waist.
अ॒सौ च॒ या न॑ उ॒र्वरादि॒मां त॒न्वं१॒॑ मम॑
अथो॑ त॒तस्य॒ यच्छिरः॒ सर्वा॒ ता रो॑म॒शा कृ॑धि
asaú ca yā́ na urvárā́d imā́ṃ tanvàm máma
átho tatásya yác chíraḥ sárvā tā́ romaśā́ kṛdhi
Make all of these grow crops of hair, you cultivated field of ours, My body, and my father's head.
खे रथ॑स्य॒ खेऽन॑सः॒ खे यु॒गस्य॑ शतक्रतो
khé ráthasya khé 'nasaḥ khé yugásya śatakrato
apālā́m indra tríṣ pūtvy ákṛṇoḥ sū́ryatvacam
Cleansing Apâlâ, Indra! thrice, thou gavest sunlike skin to her, Drawn, Ṣatakratu! through the hole of car, of wagon, and of yoke.
92: पान्त॒मा वो॒ अन्ध॑स॒ इन्द्र॑म॒भि प्र गा॑यत
pā́ntam ā́ vo ándhasa índram abhí prá gāyata
INVITE ye Indra with a song to drink your draught of Soma juice, All-conquering Ṣatakratu, most munificent of all who live.
Lauded by many, much-invoked, leader of song, renowned of old: His name is Indra, tell it forth.
इन्द्र॒ इन्नो॑ म॒हानां॑ दा॒ता वाजा॑नां नृ॒तुः
índra ín no mahā́nāṃ dātā́ vā́jānāṃ nṛtúḥ
Indra the Dancer be to us the giver of abundant strength: May he, the mighty, bring it near.
ápād u śipry ándhasaḥ sudákṣasya prahoṣíṇaḥ
Indra whose jaws are strong hath drunk of worshipping Sudaksha's draught, The Soma juice with barley mixt.
tám v abhí prā́rcaténdraṃ sómasya pītáye
Call Indra loudly with your songs of praise to drink the Soma juice. For this is what augments his stiength.
When he hath drank its gladdening drops, the God with vigour of a God Hath far surpassed all things that are.
tyám u vaḥ satrāsā́haṃ víśvāsu gīrṣv ā́yatam
Thou speedest down to succour us this ever-conquering God of yours, Him who is drawn to all our songs
The Warrior not to be restrained, the Soma-drinker ne'er o'erthrown, The Chieftain of resistless might.
शिक्षा॑ ण इन्द्र रा॒य आ पु॒रु वि॒द्वाँ ऋ॑चीषम
śíkṣā ṇa indra rāyá ā́ purú vidvā́m̐ ṛcīṣama
O Indra, send us riches, thou Omniscient, worthy of our praise: Help us in the decisive fray.
átaś cid indra ṇa úpā́ yāhi śatávājayā
Even thence, O Indra, come to us with food that gives a hundred powers, With food that gives a thousand powers.
We sought the wisdom of the wise. Ṣakra, Kine-giver, Thunder-armed! May we with steeds o’ercome in fight.
व॒यमु॑ त्वा शतक्रतो॒ गावो॒ न यव॑से॒ष्वा
vayám u tvā śatakrato gā́vo ná yávaseṣv ā́
We make thee, Ṣatakratu, find enjoyment in the songs we sing, Like cattle in the pasture lands.
For, Ṣatakratu, Thunder-armed, all that we craved, as men are wont, All that we hoped, have we attained.
Those, Son of Strength, are come to thee who cherish wishes in their hearts: O Indra, none excelleth thee.
स नो॑ वृष॒न्त्सनि॑ष्ठया॒ सं घो॒रया॑ द्रवि॒त्न्वा
sá no vṛṣan sániṣṭhayā sáṃ ghoráyā dravitnvā́
So, Hero, guard us with thy care, with thy most liberal providence, Speedy, and terrible to foes.
yás te nūnáṃ śatakratav índra dyumnítamo mádaḥ
O Ṣatakratu Indra, now rejoice with that carouse of thine Which is most splendid of them all;
yás te citráśravastamo yá indra vṛtrahántamaḥ
Even, Indra, that carouse which slays the Vritras best, most widely famed, Best giver of thy power and might.
वि॒द्मा हि यस्ते॑ अद्रिव॒स्त्वाद॑त्तः सत्य सोमपाः
vidmā́ hí yás te adrivas tvā́dattaḥ satya somapāḥ
For that which is thy gift we know, true Soma-drinker, Thunder-armed, Mighty One, amid all the folk.
इन्द्रा॑य॒ मद्व॑ने सु॒तं परि॑ ष्टोभन्तु नो॒ गिरः॑
índrāya mádvane sutám pári ṣṭobhantu no gíraḥ
For Indra, Lover of Carouse, loud be our songs about the juice: Let poets sing the song of praise.
यस्मि॒न्विश्वा॒ अधि॒ श्रियो॒ रण॑न्ति स॒प्त सं॒सदः॑
yásmin víśvā ádhi śríyo ráṇanti saptá saṃsádaḥ
We summon Indra to the draught, in whom all glories rest, in whom The seven communities rejoice.
At the Trikadrukas the Gods span sacrifice that stirs the mind: Let our songs aid and prosper it.
ā́ tvā viśantv índavaḥ samudrám iva síndhavaḥ
Let the drops pass within thee as the rivers flow into the sea: O Indra, naught excelleth thee.
vivyáktha mahinā́ vṛṣan bhakṣáṃ sómasya jāgṛve
Thou, wakeful Hero, by thy might hast taken food of Soma juice, Which, Indra, is within thee now.
अरं॑ त इन्द्र कु॒क्षये॒ सोमो॑ भवतु वृत्रहन्
áraṃ ta indra kukṣáye sómo bhavatu vṛtrahan
O Indra, Vritra-slayer, let Soma be ready for thy maw, The drops be ready for thy forms.
áram áśvāya gāyati śrutákakṣo áraṃ gáve
Now Ṣrutakaksha sings his song that cattle and the steed may come, That Indra’s very self may come.
अरं॒ हि ष्म॑ सु॒तेषु॑ णः॒ सोमे॑ष्विन्द्र॒ भूष॑सि
áraṃ hí ṣma sutéṣu ṇaḥ sómeṣv indra bhū́ṣasi
Here, Indra, thou art ready by our Soma juices shed for thee, Ṣakra, at hand that thou mayst give.
parākā́ttāc cid adrivas tvā́ṃ nakṣanta no gíraḥ
Even from far away our songs reach thee, O Caster of the Stone: May we come very close to thee.
ए॒वा ह्यसि॑ वीर॒युरे॒वा शूर॑ उ॒त स्थि॒रः
evā́ hy ási vīrayúr evā́ śū́ra utá sthiráḥ
For so thou art the hero’s Friend, a Hero, too, art thou, and strong: So may thine heart be won to us.
evā́ rātís tuvīmagha víśvebhir dhāyi dhātṛ́bhiḥ
So hath the offering, wealthiest Lord, been paid by all the worshippers: So dwell thou, Indra, even with me.
मो षु ब्र॒ह्मेव॑ तन्द्र॒युर्भुवो॑ वाजानां पते
mó ṣú brahméva tandrayúr bhúvo vājānām pate
He not thou like a slothful priest, O Lord of spoil and wealth: rejoice In the pressed Soma blent with milk.
मा न॑ इन्द्रा॒भ्या॒३॒॑दिशः॒ सूरो॑ अ॒क्तुष्वा य॑मन्
mā́ na indrābhy āā̀díśaḥ sū́ro aktúṣv ā́ yaman
O Indra, let not ill designs surround us in the sunbeams' light: This may we gain with thee for Friend.
त्वयेदि॑न्द्र यु॒जा व॒यं प्रति॑ ब्रुवीमहि॒ स्पृधः॑
tváyéd indra yujā́ vayám práti bruvīmahi spṛ́dhaḥ
With thee to help us, Indra, let us answer all our enemies: For thou art ours and we are thine.
Indra, the poets and thy friends, faithful to thee, shall loudly sing Thy praises as they follow thee.
93: úd ghéd abhí śrutā́maghaṃ vṛṣabháṃ náryāpasam
Sûrya, thou mountest up to meet the Hero famous for his wealth, Who hurls the bolt and works for man
नव॒ यो न॑व॒तिं पुरो॑ बि॒भेद॑ बा॒ह्वो॑जसा
náva yó navatím púro bibhéda bāhvòjasā
Him who with might of both his arms brake nine-and-ninety castles down, Slew Vr̥itra and smote Ahi dead.
sá na índraḥ śiváḥ sákhā́śvāvad gómad yávamat
This Indra is our gracious Friend. He sends us in a full broad stream Riches in horses, kine, and corn.
yád adyá kác ca vṛtrahann udágā abhí sūrya
Whatever, Vr̥itra-slayer! thou, Sûrya, hast risen upon to-day, That, Indra, all is in thy power.
यद्वा॑ प्रवृद्ध सत्पते॒ न म॑रा॒ इति॒ मन्य॑से
yád vā pravṛddha satpate ná marā íti mányase
When, Mighty One, Lord of the brave, thou thinkest thus, I shall not die, That thought of thine is true indeed.
ये सोमा॑सः परा॒वति॒ ये अ॑र्वा॒वति॑ सुन्वि॒रे
yé sómāsaḥ parāváti yé arvāváti sunviré
Thou, Indra, goest unto all Soma libations shed for thee, Both far away and near at hand.
tám índraṃ vājayāmasi mahé vṛtrā́ya hántave
We make this Indra very strong to strike the mighty Vr̥itra dead: A vigorous Hero shall he be.
इन्द्रः॒ स दाम॑ने कृ॒त ओजि॑ष्ठः॒ स मदे॑ हि॒तः
índraḥ sá dā́mane kṛtá ójiṣṭhaḥ sá máde hitáḥ
Indra was made for giving, set, most mighty, o'er the joyous draught. Bright, meet for Soma, famed in song.
गि॒रा वज्रो॒ न सम्भृ॑तः॒ सब॑लो॒ अन॑पच्युतः
girā́ vájro ná sámbhṛtaḥ sábalo ánapacyutaḥ
By song as 'twere, the powerful bolt which none may parry was prepared Lofty, invincible he grew.
दु॒र्गे चि॑न्नः सु॒गं कृ॑धि गृणा॒न इ॑न्द्र गिर्वणः
durgé cin naḥ sugáṃ kṛdhi gṛṇāná indra girvaṇaḥ
Indra, Song-lover, lauded, make even in the wilds fair ways for us, Whenever, Maghavan, thou wilt.
यस्य॑ ते॒ नू चि॑दा॒दिशं॒ न मि॒नन्ति॑ स्व॒राज्य॑म्
yásya te nū́ cid ādíśaṃ ná minánti svarā́jyam
Thou whose commandment and behest of sovran sway none disregards, Neither audacious man nor God.
अधा॑ ते॒ अप्र॑तिष्कुतं दे॒वी शुष्मं॑ सपर्यतः
ádhā te ápratiṣkutaṃ devī́ śúṣmaṃ saparyataḥ
And both these Goddesses, Earth, Heaven, Lord of the beauteous helm! revere Thy might which no one may resist.
tvám etád adhārayaḥ kṛṣṇā́su róhiṇīṣu ca
Thou in the black cows and the red and in the cows with spotted skin This white milk hast deposited.
वि यदहे॒रध॑ त्वि॒षो विश्वे॑ दे॒वासो॒ अक्र॑मुः
ví yád áher ádha tviṣó víśve devā́so ákramuḥ
When in their terror all the Gods shrank from the Dragon’s furious might, Fear of the monster fell on them.
ā́d u me nivaró bhuvad vṛtrahā́diṣṭa paúṃsyam
Then he was my Defender, then, Invincible, whose foe is not, The Vritra-slayer showed his might.
श्रु॒तं वो॑ वृत्र॒हन्त॑मं॒ प्र शर्धं॑ चर्षणी॒नाम्
śrutáṃ vo vṛtrahántamam prá śárdhaṃ carṣaṇīnā́m
Him your best Vritra-slayer, him the famous Champion of mankind I urge to great munificence,
ayā́ dhiyā́ ca gavyayā́ púruṇāman púruṣṭuta
To come, Much-lauded! Many-named! with this same thought that longs for milk, Whene’er the Soma juice is shed.
bodhínmanā íd astu no vṛtrahā́ bhū́ryāsutiḥ
Much-honoured by libations, may the Vritra-slayer wake for us: May Ṣakra listen to our prayers.
कया॒ त्वं न॑ ऊ॒त्याभि प्र म॑न्दसे वृषन्
káyā tváṃ na ūtyā́bhí prá mandase vṛṣan
O Hero, with what aid dost thou delight us, with what succour bring Riches to those who worship thee?
कस्य॒ वृषा॑ सु॒ते सचा॑ नि॒युत्वा॑न्वृष॒भो र॑णत्
kásya vṛ́ṣā suté sácā niyútvān vṛṣabhó raṇat
With whose libation joys the Strong, the Hero with his team who quells The foe, to drink the Soma juice?
अ॒भी षु ण॒स्त्वं र॒यिं म॑न्दसा॒नः स॑ह॒स्रिण॑म्
abhī́ ṣú ṇas tváṃ rayím mandasānáḥ sahasríṇam
Rejoicing in thy spirit bring thousandfold opulence to us: Enrich thy votary with gifts.
पत्नी॑वन्तः सु॒ता इ॒म उ॒शन्तो॑ यन्ति वी॒तये॑
pátnīvantaḥ sutā́ imá uśánto yanti vītáye
These juices with their wedded wives flow to enjoyment lovingly: To waters speeds the restless one.
Presented strengthening gifts have sent Indra away at sacrifice, With might, unto the cleansing bath.
These two who share his feast, Bay Steeds with golden manes, shall bring him to The banquet that is laid for him.
तुभ्यं॒ सोमाः॑ सु॒ता इ॒मे स्ती॒र्णं ब॒र्हिर्वि॑भावसो
túbhyaṃ sómāḥ sutā́ imé stīrṇám barhír vibhāvaso
For thee, O Lord of Light, are shed these Soma-drops, and grass is strewn: Bring Indra to his worshippers.
आ ते॒ दक्षं॒ वि रो॑च॒ना दध॒द्रत्ना॒ वि दा॒शुषे॑
ā́ te dákṣaṃ ví rocanā́ dádhad rátnā ví dāśúṣe
May Indra give thee skill and lights of heaven, wealth to his votary And priests who praise him: laud ye him.
ā́ te dadhāmīndriyám ukthā́ víśvā śatakrato
O Ṣatakratu, wondrous strength and all our lauds I bring to thee: Be gracious to thy worshippers.
bhadrám-bhadraṃ na ā́ bharéṣam ū́rjaṃ śatakrato
Bring to us all things excellent, O Ṣatakratu, food and strength; For, Indra, thou art kind to us.
स नो॒ विश्वा॒न्या भ॑र सुवि॒तानि॑ शतक्रतो
sá no víśvāny ā́ bhara suvitā́ni śatakrato
O Ṣatakratu, bring to us all blessings, all felicity: For, Indra, thou art kind to us.
Bearing the Soma juice we call, best Vritra-slayer, unto thee: For, Indra, thou art kind to us.
उप॑ नो॒ हरि॑भिः सु॒तं या॒हि म॑दानां पते
úpa no háribhiḥ sutáṃ yāhí madānām pate
Come, Lord of rapturous joys, to our libation with thy Bay Steeds, come To our libation with thy Steeds.
द्वि॒ता यो वृ॑त्र॒हन्त॑मो वि॒द इन्द्रः॑ श॒तक्र॑तुः
dvitā́ yó vṛtrahántamo vidá índraḥ śatákratuḥ
Known as best Vritra-slayer erst, as Indra Ṣatakratu, come With Bay Steeds to the juice we shed.
tváṃ hí vṛtrahann eṣām pātā́ sómānām ási
O Vritra-slayer, thou art he who drinks these drops of Soma: come With Bay Steeds to the juice we shed.
इन्द्र॑ इ॒षे द॑दातु न ऋभु॒क्षण॑मृ॒भुं र॒यिम्
índra iṣé dadātu na ṛbhukṣáṇam ṛbhúṃ rayím
May Indra give, to aid us, wealth handy that rules the Skilful Ones: Yea, may the Strong give potent wealth.
94: gaúr dhayati marútāṃ śravasyúr mātā́ maghónām
THE Cow, the famous Mother of the wealthy Maruts, pours her milk: Both horses of the cars are yoked,–
यस्या॑ दे॒वा उ॒पस्थे॑ व्र॒ता विश्वे॑ धा॒रय॑न्ते
yásyā devā́ upásthe vratā́ víśve dhāráyante
She in whose bosom all the Gods, and Sun and Moon for men to see, Maintain their everlasting Laws.
तत्सु नो॒ विश्वे॑ अ॒र्य आ सदा॑ गृणन्ति का॒रवः॑
tát sú no víśve aryá ā́ sádā gṛṇanti kārávaḥ
This all the pious sing to us, and sacred poets evermore: The Maruts to the Soma-draught
अस्ति॒ सोमो॑ अ॒यं सु॒तः पिब॑न्त्यस्य म॒रुतः॑
ásti sómo ayáṃ sutáḥ píbanty asya marútaḥ
Here is the Soma ready pressed of this the Maruts drink, of this Self-luminous the Aṣvins drink.
पिब॑न्ति मि॒त्रो अ॑र्य॒मा तना॑ पू॒तस्य॒ वरु॑णः
píbanti mitró aryamā́ tánā pūtásya váruṇaḥ
Of this, moreover, purified, set in three places, procreant, Drink Varuṇa, Mitra, Aryaman.
उ॒तो न्व॑स्य॒ जोष॒माँ इन्द्रः॑ सु॒तस्य॒ गोम॑तः
utó nv àsya jóṣam ā́m̐ índraḥ sutásya gómataḥ
And Indra, like the Herald Priest, desirous of the milky juice, At early morn will quaff thereof.
kád atviṣanta sūráyas tirá ā́pa iva srídhaḥ
When have the Princes gleamed and shone through waters as through troops of foes? When hasten they whose might is pure?
kád vo adyá mahā́nāṃ devā́nām ávo vṛṇe
What favour do I claim this day of you great Deities, you who are Wondrously splendid in yourselves?
आ ये विश्वा॒ पार्थि॑वानि प॒प्रथ॑न्रोच॒ना दि॒वः
ā́ yé víśvā pā́rthivāni papráthan rocanā́ diváḥ
I call, to drink the Soma, those Maruts who spread all realms of earth And luminous regions of the sky.
त्यान्नु पू॒तद॑क्षसो दि॒वो वो॑ मरुतो हुवे
tyā́n nú pūtádakṣaso divó vo maruto huve
You, even such, pure in your might, you, O ye Maruts, I invoke From heaven to drink this Soma juice.
त्यान्नु ये वि रोद॑सी तस्त॒भुर्म॒रुतो॑ हुवे
tyā́n nú yé ví ródasī tastabhúr marúto huve
The Maruts, those who have sustained and propped the heavens and earth apart, I call to drink this Soma juice.
त्यं नु मारु॑तं ग॒णं गि॑रि॒ष्ठां वृष॑णं हुवे
tyáṃ nú mā́rutaṃ gaṇáṃ giriṣṭhā́ṃ vṛ́ṣaṇaṃ huve
That vigorous baud of Maruts that abideth in the mountains, I Invoke to drink this Soma juice.
95: आ त्वा॒ गिरो॑ र॒थीरि॒वास्थुः॑ सु॒तेषु॑ गिर्वणः
अ॒भि त्वा॒ सम॑नूष॒तेन्द्र॑ व॒त्सं न मा॒तरः॑
ā́ tvā gíro rathī́r ivā́sthuḥ sutéṣu girvaṇaḥ
abhí tvā sám anūṣaténdra vatsáṃ ná mātáraḥ
SONG-LOVER! like a charioteer come songs to thee when Soma flows. O Indra, they have called to thee as mother-kine unto their calves.
आ त्वा॑ शु॒क्रा अ॑चुच्यवुः सु॒तास॑ इन्द्र गिर्वणः
पिबा॒ त्व१॒॑स्यान्ध॑स॒ इन्द्र॒ विश्वा॑सु ते हि॒तम्
ā́ tvā śukrā́ acucyavuḥ sutā́sa indra girvaṇaḥ
píbā tv àsyā́ndhasa índra víśvāsu te hitám
Bright juices hitherward have sped thee, Indra, Lover of the Song. Drink, Indra, of this flowing sap: in every house 'tis set for thee.
पिबा॒ सोमं॒ मदा॑य॒ कमिन्द्र॑ श्ये॒नाभृ॑तं सु॒तम्
त्वं हि शश्व॑तीनां॒ पती॒ राजा॑ वि॒शामसि॑
píbā sómam mádāya kám índra śyenā́bhṛtaṃ sutám
tváṃ hí śáśvatīnām pátī rā́jā viśā́m ási
Drink Soma to inspirit thee, juice, Indra, which the Falcon brought: For thou art King and Sovran Lord of all the families of men.
श्रु॒धी हवं॑ तिर॒श्च्या इन्द्र॒ यस्त्वा॑ सप॒र्यति॑
śrudhī́ hávaṃ tiraścyā́ índra yás tvā saparyáti
suvī́ryasya gómato rāyás pūrdhi mahā́m̐ asi
O Indra, hear Tiraṣchî's call, the call of him who serveth thee. Satisfy him with wealth of kine and valiant offspring: Great art thou.
índra yás te návīyasīṃ gíram mandrā́m ájījanat
For he, O Indra, hath produced for thee the newest gladdening song, A hymn that springs from careful thought, ancient, and full of sacred truth.
तमु॑ ष्टवाम॒ यं गिर॒ इन्द्र॑मु॒क्थानि॑ वावृ॒धुः
tám u ṣṭavāma yáṃ gíra índram ukthā́ni vāvṛdhúḥ
That Indra will we laud whom songs and hymns of praise have magnified. Striving to win, we celebrate his many deeds of hero might.
एतो॒ न्विन्द्रं॒ स्तवा॑म शु॒द्धं शु॒द्धेन॒ साम्ना॑
éto nv índraṃ stávāma śuddháṃ śuddhéna sā́mnā
śuddhaír ukthaír vāvṛdhvā́ṃsaṃ śuddhá āśī́rvān mamattu
Come now and let us glorify pure Indra with pure Sâma hymns. Let the pure milky draught delight him strengthened by pure songs of praise.
इन्द्र॑ शु॒द्धो न॒ आ ग॑हि शु॒द्धः शु॒द्धाभि॑रू॒तिभिः॑
शु॒द्धो र॒यिं नि धा॑रय शु॒द्धो म॑मद्धि सो॒म्यः
índra śuddhó na ā́ gahi śuddháḥ śuddhā́bhir ūtíbhiḥ
śuddhó rayíṃ ní dhāraya śuddhó mamaddhi somyáḥ
O Indra, come thou pure to us, with pure assistance, pure thyself. Pure, send thou riches down to us, and, meet for Soma, pure, be glad.
इन्द्र॑ शु॒द्धो हि नो॑ र॒यिं शु॒द्धो रत्ना॑नि दा॒शुषे॑
शु॒द्धो वृ॒त्राणि॑ जिघ्नसे शु॒द्धो वाजं॑ सिषाससि
índra śuddhó hí no rayíṃ śuddhó rátnāni dāśúṣe
śuddhó vṛtrā́ṇi jighnase śuddhó vā́jaṃ siṣāsasi
O Indra, pure, vouchsafe us wealth, and, pure, enrich the worshipper. Pure, thou dost strike the Vr̥itras dead, and strivest, pure, to win the spoil.
96: अ॒स्मा उ॒षास॒ आति॑रन्त॒ याम॒मिन्द्रा॑य॒ नक्त॒मूर्म्याः॑ सु॒वाचः॑
अ॒स्मा आपो॑ मा॒तरः॑ स॒प्त त॑स्थु॒र्नृभ्य॒स्तरा॑य॒ सिन्ध॑वः सुपा॒राः
asmā́ uṣā́sa ā́tiranta yā́mam índrāya náktam ū́rmyāḥ suvā́caḥ
asmā́ ā́po mātáraḥ saptá tasthur nṛ́bhyas tárāya síndhavaḥ supārā́ḥ
FOR him the Mornings made their courses longer, and Nights with pleasant voices spake to Indra. For him the Floods stood still, the Seven Mothers, Streams easy for the heroes to pass over.
अति॑विद्धा विथु॒रेणा॑ चि॒दस्त्रा॒ त्रिः स॒प्त सानु॒ संहि॑ता गिरी॒णाम्
न तद्दे॒वो न मर्त्य॑स्तुतुर्या॒द्यानि॒ प्रवृ॑द्धो वृष॒भश्च॒कार॑
átividdhā vithuréṇā cid ástrā tríḥ saptá sā́nu sáṃhitā girīṇā́m
ná tád devó ná mártyas tuturyād yā́ni právṛddho vṛṣabháś cakā́ra
The Darter penetrated, though in trouble, thrice-seven close-pressed ridges of the mountains. Neither might God nor mortal man accomplish what the Strong Hero wrought in full-grown vigour.
इन्द्र॑स्य॒ वज्र॑ आय॒सो निमि॑श्ल॒ इन्द्र॑स्य बा॒ह्वोर्भूयि॑ष्ठ॒मोजः॑
शी॒र्षन्निन्द्र॑स्य॒ क्रत॑वो निरे॒क आ॒सन्नेष॑न्त॒ श्रुत्या॑ उपा॒के
índrasya vájra āyasó nímiśla índrasya bāhvór bhū́yiṣṭham ójaḥ
śīrṣánn índrasya krátavo nireká āsánn éṣanta śrútyā upāké
The mightiest force is Indra's bolt of iron when firmly grasped in both the arms of Indra. His head and mouth have powers that pass all others, and all his people hasten near to listen.
मन्ये॑ त्वा य॒ज्ञियं॑ य॒ज्ञिया॑नां॒ मन्ये॑ त्वा॒ च्यव॑न॒मच्यु॑तानाम्
मन्ये॑ त्वा॒ सत्व॑नामिन्द्र के॒तुं मन्ये॑ त्वा वृष॒भं च॑र्षणी॒नाम्
mánye tvā yajñíyaṃ yajñíyānām mánye tvā cyávanam ácyutānām
mánye tvā sátvanām indra ketúm mánye tvā vṛṣabháṃ carṣaṇīnā́m
I count thee as the Holiest of the Holy, the caster-down of what hath ne'er been shaken. I count thee as the Banner of the heroes, I count thee as the Chief of all men living.
आ यद्वज्रं॑ बा॒ह्वोरि॑न्द्र॒ धत्से॑ मद॒च्युत॒मह॑ये॒ हन्त॒वा उ॑
प्र पर्व॑ता॒ अन॑वन्त॒ प्र गावः॒ प्र ब्र॒ह्माणो॑ अभि॒नक्ष॑न्त॒ इन्द्र॑म्
ā́ yád vájram bāhvór indra dhátse madacyútam áhaye hántavā́ u
prá párvatā ánavanta prá gā́vaḥ prá brahmā́ṇo abhinákṣanta índram
What time, O Indra, in thine arms thou tookest thy wildly rushing bolt to Slay the Dragon, The mountains roared, the cattle loudly bellowed, the Brahmans with their hymns drew nigh to Indra.
तमु॑ ष्टवाम॒ य इ॒मा ज॒जान॒ विश्वा॑ जा॒तान्यव॑राण्यस्मात्
इन्द्रे॑ण मि॒त्रं दि॑धिषेम गी॒र्भिरुपो॒ नमो॑भिर्वृष॒भं वि॑शेम
tám u ṣṭavāma yá imā́ jajā́na víśvā jātā́ny ávarāṇy asmāt
índreṇa mitráṃ didhiṣema gīrbhír úpo námobhir vṛṣabháṃ viśema
Let us praise him who made these worlds and creatures, all things that after him sprang into being. May we win Mitra with our songs, and Indra, and. wait upon our Lord with adoration.
वृ॒त्रस्य॑ त्वा श्व॒सथा॒दीष॑माणा॒ विश्वे॑ दे॒वा अ॑जहु॒र्ये सखा॑यः
म॒रुद्भि॑रिन्द्र स॒ख्यं ते॑ अ॒स्त्वथे॒मा विश्वाः॒ पृत॑ना जयासि
vṛtrásya tvā śvasáthād ī́ṣamāṇā víśve devā́ ajahur yé sákhāyaḥ
marúdbhir indra sakhyáṃ te astv áthemā́ víśvāḥ pṛ́tanā jayāsi
Flying in terror from the snort of Vr̥itra, all Deities who were thy friends forsook thee. So, Indra, be thy friendship with the Maruts: in all these battles thou shalt be the victor.
त्रिः ष॒ष्टिस्त्वा॑ म॒रुतो॑ वावृधा॒ना उ॒स्रा इ॑व रा॒शयो॑ य॒ज्ञिया॑सः
उप॒ त्वेमः॑ कृ॒धि नो॑ भाग॒धेयं॒ शुष्मं॑ त ए॒ना ह॒विषा॑ विधेम
tríḥ ṣaṣṭís tvā marúto vāvṛdhānā́ usrā́ iva rāśáyo yajñíyāsaḥ
úpa tvémaḥ kṛdhí no bhāgadhéyaṃ śúṣmaṃ ta enā́ havíṣā vidhema
Thrice-sixty Maruts, waxing strong, were with thee, like piles of beaming light, worthy of worship. We come to thee: grant us a happy portion. Let us adore thy might with this oblation.
ति॒ग्ममायु॑धं म॒रुता॒मनी॑कं॒ कस्त॑ इन्द्र॒ प्रति॒ वज्रं॑ दधर्ष
अ॒ना॒यु॒धासो॒ असु॑रा अदे॒वाश्च॒क्रेण॒ ताँ अप॑ वप ऋजीषिन्
tigmám ā́yudham marútām ánīkaṃ kás ta indra práti vájraṃ dadharṣa
anāyudhā́so ásurā adevā́ś cakréṇa tā́m̐ ápa vapa ṛjīṣin
A sharpened weapon is the host of Maruts. Who, Indra, dares withstand thy bolt of thunder? Weaponless are the Asuras, the godless: scatter them with thy wheel, Impetuous Hero.
म॒ह उ॒ग्राय॑ त॒वसे॑ सुवृ॒क्तिं प्रेर॑य शि॒वत॑माय प॒श्वः
गिर्वा॑हसे॒ गिर॒ इन्द्रा॑य पू॒र्वीर्धे॒हि त॒न्वे॑ कु॒विद॒ङ्ग वेद॑त्
mahá ugrā́ya taváse suvṛktím préraya śivátamāya paśváḥ
gírvāhase gíra índrāya pūrvī́r dhehí tanvè kuvíd aṅgá védat
To him the Strong and Mighty, most auspicious, send up the beauteous hymn for sake of cattle. Lay on his body many songs for Indra invoked with song, for will not he regard them
उ॒क्थवा॑हसे वि॒भ्वे॑ मनी॒षां द्रुणा॒ न पा॒रमी॑रया न॒दीना॑म्
नि स्पृ॑श धि॒या त॒न्वि॑ श्रु॒तस्य॒ जुष्ट॑तरस्य कु॒विद॒ङ्ग वेद॑त्
ukthávāhase vibhvè manīṣā́ṃ drúṇā ná pārám īrayā nadī́nām
ní spṛśa dhiyā́ tanv .ì śrutásya júṣṭatarasya kuvíd aṅgá védat
To him, the Mighty, who accepts laudation, send forth thy thought as by a boat o’er rivers, Stir with thy hymn the body of the Famous and Dearest One, for will not he regard it?
तद्वि॑विड्ढि॒ यत्त॒ इन्द्रो॒ जुजो॑षत्स्तु॒हि सु॑ष्टु॒तिं नम॒सा वि॑वास
उप॑ भूष जरित॒र्मा रु॑वण्यः श्रा॒वया॒ वाचं॑ कु॒विद॒ङ्ग वेद॑त्
tád viviḍḍhi yát ta índro jújoṣat stuhí suṣṭutíṃ námasā́ vivāsa
úpa bhūṣa jaritar mā́ ruvaṇyaḥ śrāváyā vā́caṃ kuvíd aṅgá védat

Serve him with gifts of thine which Indra welcomes: praise with fair praise, invite him with thine homage. Draw near, O singer, and refrain from outcry. Make thy voice heard, for will not he regard it?
अव॑ द्र॒प्सो अं॑शु॒मती॑मतिष्ठदिया॒नः कृ॒ष्णो द॒शभिः॑ स॒हस्रैः॑
áva drapsó aṃśumátīm atiṣṭhad iyānáḥ kṛṣṇó daśábhiḥ sahásraiḥ
ā́vat tám índraḥ śácyā dhámantam ápa snéhitīr nṛmáṇā adhatta
The Black Drop sank in Anṣumatîs bosom, advancing with ten thousand round about it. Indra with might longed for it as it panted: the hero-hearted laid aside his weapons.
नभो॒ न कृ॒ष्णम॑वतस्थि॒वांस॒मिष्या॑मि वो वृषणो॒ युध्य॑ता॒जौ
drapsám apaśyaṃ víṣuṇe cárantam upahvaré nadyò aṃśumátyāḥ
nábho ná kṛṣṇám avatasthivā́ṃsam íṣyāmi vo vṛṣaṇo yúdhyatājaú
I saw the Drop in the far distance moving, on the slope bank of Anṣumatîs river, Like a black cloud that sank into the water. Heroes, I send you forth. Go, fight in battle.
ádha drapsó aṃśumátyā upásthé 'dhārayat tanvàṃ titviṣāṇáḥ
víśo ádevīr abhy āā̀cárantīr bṛ́haspátinā yujéndraḥ sasāhe
And then the Drop in Anṣumatîs bosom, splendid with light, assumed its proper body; And Indra, with Br̥ihaspati to aid him, conquered the godless tribes that came against him.
त्वं ह॒ त्यत्स॒प्तभ्यो॒ जाय॑मानोऽश॒त्रुभ्यो॑ अभवः॒ शत्रु॑रिन्द्र
गू॒ळ्हे द्यावा॑पृथि॒वी अन्व॑विन्दो विभु॒मद्भ्यो॒ भुव॑नेभ्यो॒ रणं॑ धाः
tváṃ ha tyát saptábhyo jā́yamāno 'śatrúbhyo abhavaḥ śátrur indra
gūḷhé dyā́vāpṛthivī́ ánv avindo vibhumádbhyo bhúvanebhyo ráṇaṃ dhāḥ
Then, at thy birth, thou wast the foeman, Indra, of those the seven who ne'er had met a rival. The hidden Pair, the Heaven and Earth, thou foundest, and to the mighty worlds thou gavest pleasure.
त्वं ह॒ त्यद॑प्रतिमा॒नमोजो॒ वज्रे॑ण वज्रिन्धृषि॒तो ज॑घन्थ
त्वं शुष्ण॒स्यावा॑तिरो॒ वध॑त्रै॒स्त्वं गा इ॑न्द्र॒ शच्येद॑विन्दः
tváṃ ha tyád apratimānám ójo vájreṇa vajrin dhṛṣitó jaghantha
tváṃ śúṣṇasyā́vātiro vádhatrais tváṃ gā́ indra śácyéd avindaḥ

So, Thunder-armed! thou with thy bolt of thunder didst boldly smite that power which none might equal; With weapons broughtest low the phght of Sushna, and, Indra, foundest by thy strength the cattle.
त्वं ह॒ त्यद्वृ॑षभ चर्षणी॒नां घ॒नो वृ॒त्राणां॑ तवि॒षो ब॑भूथ
tváṃ ha tyád vṛṣabha carṣaṇīnā́ṃ ghanó vṛtrā́ṇāṃ taviṣó babhūtha
tváṃ síndhūm̐r asṛjas tastabhānā́n tvám apó ajayo dāsápatnīḥ
Then wast thou, Chieftain of all living mortals, the very mighty slayer of the Vritras. Then didst thou set the obstructed rivers flowing, and win the floods that were enthralled by Dâsas.
स सु॒क्रतू॒ रणि॑ता॒ यः सु॒तेष्वनु॑त्तमन्यु॒र्यो अहे॑व रे॒वान्
य एक॒ इन्नर्यपां॑सि॒ कर्ता॒ स वृ॑त्र॒हा प्रतीद॒न्यमा॑हुः
sá sukrátū ráṇitā yáḥ sutéṣv ánuttamanyur yó áheva revā́n
yá éka ín náry ápāṃsi kártā sá vṛtrahā́ prátī́d anyám āhuḥ
Most wise is he, rejoicing in libations, splendid as day, resistless in his anger. He only doth great deeds, the only Hero, sole Vritra-slayer he, with none beside him.
स प्रा॑वि॒ता म॒घवा॑ नोऽधिव॒क्ता स वाज॑स्य श्रव॒स्य॑स्य दा॒ता
sá vṛtrahéndraś carṣaṇīdhṛ́t táṃ suṣṭutyā́ hávyaṃ huvema
sá prāvitā́ maghávā no 'dhivaktā́ sá vā́jasya śravasyàsya dātā́
Indra is Vritra’s slayer, man’s sustainer: he must be called; with fair praise let us call him. Maghavan is our Helper, our Protector, giver of spoil and wealth to make us famous.
स वृ॑त्र॒हेन्द्र॑ ऋभु॒क्षाः स॒द्यो ज॑ज्ञा॒नो हव्यो॑ बभूव
कृ॒ण्वन्नपां॑सि॒ नर्या॑ पु॒रूणि॒ सोमो॒ न पी॒तो हव्यः॒ सखि॑भ्यः
sá vṛtrahéndra ṛbhukṣā́ḥ sadyó jajñānó hávyo babhūva
kṛṇvánn ápāṃsi náryā purū́ṇi sómo ná pītó hávyaḥ sákhibhyaḥ
This Indra, Vritra-slayer, this Ribhukshan, even at his birth, was meet for invocation. Doer of many deeds for man’s advantage, like Soma quaffed, for friends we must invoke him.
97: या इ॑न्द्र॒ भुज॒ आभ॑रः॒ स्व॑र्वाँ॒ असु॑रेभ्यः
स्तो॒तार॒मिन्म॑घवन्नस्य वर्धय॒ ये च॒ त्वे वृ॒क्तब॑र्हिषः
yā́ indra bhúja ā́bharaḥ svàrvām̐ ásurebhyaḥ
stotā́ram ín maghavann asya vardhaya yé ca tvé vṛktábarhiṣaḥ
O INDRA, Lord of Light, what joys thou broughtest from the Asuras, Prosper therewith, O Maghavan, him who lauds that deed, and those whose grass is trimmed for thee.
यज॑माने सुन्व॒ति दक्षि॑णावति॒ तस्मि॒न्तं धे॑हि॒ मा प॒णौ
yám indra dadhiṣé tvám áśvaṃ gā́m bhāgám ávyayam
yájamāne sunvatí dákṣiṇāvati tásmin táṃ dhehi mā́ paṇaú
The unwasting share of steeds and kine which, Indra, thou hast fast secured, Grant to the worshipper who presses Soma and gives guerdon, not unto the churl.
स्वैः ष एवै॑र्मुमुर॒त्पोष्यं॑ र॒यिं स॑नु॒तर्धे॑हि॒ तं ततः॑
svaíḥ ṣá évair mumurat póṣyaṃ rayíṃ sanutár dhehi táṃ tátaḥ
The riteless, godless man who sleeps, O Indra, his unbroken sleep, – May he by following his own devices die. Hide from him wealth that nourishes.
अत॑स्त्वा गी॒र्भिर्द्यु॒गदि॑न्द्र के॒शिभिः॑ सु॒तावाँ॒ आ वि॑वासति
yác chakrā́si parāváti yád arvāváti vṛtrahan
átas tvā gīrbhír dyugád indra keśíbhiḥ sutā́vām̐ ā́ vivāsati
Whether, O Ṣakra, thou be far, or, Vritra-slayer, near at hand, Thence by heaven-reaching songs he who hath pressed the juice invites thee with thy long-maned Steeds.
यत्पार्थि॑वे॒ सद॑ने वृत्रहन्तम॒ यद॒न्तरि॑क्ष॒ आ ग॑हि
yád vā́si rocané diváḥ samudrásyā́dhi viṣṭápi
yát pā́rthive sádane vṛtrahantama yád antárikṣa ā́ gahi
Whether thou art in heaven's bright sphere, or in the basin of the sea; Whether, chief Vr̥itra-slayer, in some place on earth, or in the firmament, approach.
स नः॒ सोमे॑षु सोमपाः सु॒तेषु॑ शवसस्पते
sá naḥ sómeṣu somapāḥ sutéṣu śavasas pate
Thou Soma-drinker, Lord of Strength, beside our flowing Soma juice Delight us with thy bounty rich in pleasantness, O Indra, with abundant wealth.
मा न॑ इन्द्र॒ परा॑ वृण॒ग्भवा॑ नः सध॒माद्यः॑
त्वं न॑ ऊ॒ती त्वमिन्न॒ आप्यं॒ मा न॑ इन्द्र॒ परा॑ वृणक्
mā́ na indra párā vṛṇag bhávā naḥ sadhamā́dyaḥ
tváṃ na ūtī́ tvám ín na ā́pyam mā́ na indra párā vṛṇak
O Indra, turn us not away: be the companion of our feast. For thou art our protection, yea, thou art our kin: O Indra, turn us not away.
अ॒स्मे इ॑न्द्र॒ सचा॑ सु॒ते नि ष॑दा पी॒तये॒ मधु॑
कृ॒धी ज॑रि॒त्रे म॑घव॒न्नवो॑ म॒हद॒स्मे इ॑न्द्र॒ सचा॑ सु॒ते
asmé indra sácā suté ní ṣadā pītáye mádhu
kṛdhī́ jaritré maghavann ávo mahád asmé indra sácā suté
Sit down with us, O Indra, sit beside the juice to drink the meath. Show forth great favour to the singer, Maghavan; Indra, with us, beside the juice.
न त्वा॑ दे॒वास॑ आशत॒ न मर्त्या॑सो अद्रिवः
विश्वा॑ जा॒तानि॒ शव॑साभि॒भूर॑सि॒ न त्वा॑ दे॒वास॑ आशत
ná tvā devā́sa āśata ná mártyāso adrivaḥ
víśvā jātā́ni śávasābhibhū́r asi ná tvā devā́sa āśata
O Caster of the Stone, nor Gods nor mortals have attained to thee. Thou in thy might surpassest all that hath been made: the Gods have not attained to thee.
विश्वाः॒ पृत॑ना अभि॒भूत॑रं॒ नरं॑ स॒जूस्त॑तक्षु॒रिन्द्रं॑ जज॒नुश्च॑ रा॒जसे॑
क्रत्वा॒ वरि॑ष्ठं॒ वर॑ आ॒मुरि॑मु॒तोग्रमोजि॑ष्ठं त॒वसं॑ तर॒स्विन॑म्
sajū́s tatakṣur índraṃ jajanúś ca rājáse
krátvā váriṣṭhaṃ vára āmúrim utógrám ójiṣṭhaṃ tavásaṃ tarasvínam

Of one accord they made and formed for kingship Indra, the Hero who in all encounters overcometh, Most eminent for power, destroyer in the conflict, fierce and exceeding strong, stalwart and full of vigour.
स्व॑र्पतिं॒ यदीं॑ वृ॒धे धृ॒तव्र॑तो॒ ह्योज॑सा॒ समू॒तिभिः॑
sám īṃ rebhā́so asvarann índraṃ sómasya pītáye
svàrpatiṃ yád īṃ vṛdhé dhṛtávrato hy ójasā sám ūtíbhiḥ
Bards joined in song to Indra so that he might drink the Soma juice, The Lord of Light, that he whose laws stand fast might aid with power and with the help he gives.
ने॒मिं न॑मन्ति॒ चक्ष॑सा मे॒षं विप्रा॑ अभि॒स्वरा॑
सु॒दी॒तयो॑ वो अ॒द्रुहोऽपि॒ कर्णे॑ तर॒स्विनः॒ समृक्व॑भिः
nemíṃ namanti cákṣasā meṣáṃ víprā abhisvárā

He comes by straightest paths, as ministering Priest, to taste the sacrificial gifts. Then, Lord of harnessed teams! drink of the twofold draught, bright Soma mingled with the milk.
बण्म॒हाँ अ॑सि सूर्य॒ बळा॑दित्य म॒हाँ अ॑सि
म॒हस्ते॑ स॒तो म॑हि॒मा प॑नस्यते॒ऽद्धा दे॑व म॒हाँ अ॑सि
báṇ mahā́m̐ asi sūrya báḷ āditya mahā́m̐ asi
mahás te sató mahimā́ panasyate 'ddhā́ deva mahā́m̐ asi
Verily, Sûrya, thou art great; truly, Âditya, thou art great. As thou art great indeed, thy greatness is admired: yea, verily, thou, God, art great.
बट् सू॑र्य॒ श्रव॑सा म॒हाँ अ॑सि स॒त्रा दे॑व म॒हाँ अ॑सि
báṭ sūrya śrávasā mahā́m̐ asi satrā́ deva mahā́m̐ asi
mahnā́ devā́nām asuryàḥ puróhito vibhú jyótir ádābhyam
Yea, Sûrya, thou art great in fame: thou evermore, O God, art great. Thou by thy greatness art the Gods' High Priest, divine, far-spread unconquerable light.
इ॒यं या नीच्य॒र्किणी॑ रू॒पा रोहि॑ण्या कृ॒ता
iyáṃ yā́ nī́cy arkíṇī rūpā́ róhiṇyā kṛtā́
citréva práty adarśy āyaty àntár daśásu bāhúṣu
She yonder, bending lowly down, clothed in red hues and rich in rays, Is seen, advancing as it were with various tints, amid the ten surrounding arms.
प्र॒जा ह॑ ति॒स्रो अ॒त्याय॑मीयु॒र्न्य१॒॑न्या अ॒र्कम॒भितो॑ विविश्रे
बृ॒हद्ध॑ तस्थौ॒ भुव॑नेष्व॒न्तः पव॑मानो ह॒रित॒ आ वि॑वेश
prajā́ ha tisró atyā́yam īyur ny ànyā́ arkám abhíto viviśre
bṛhád dha tasthau bhúvaneṣv antáḥ pávamāno haríta ā́ viveśa
Past and gone are three mortal generations: the fourth and last into the Sun hath entered. He mid the worlds his lofty place hath taken. Into green plants is gone the Purifying.
मा॒ता रु॒द्राणां॑ दुहि॒ता वसू॑नां॒ स्वसा॑दि॒त्याना॑म॒मृत॑स्य॒ नाभिः॑
प्र नु वो॑चं चिकि॒तुषे॒ जना॑य॒ मा गामना॑गा॒मदि॑तिं वधिष्ट
mātā́ rudrā́ṇāṃ duhitā́ vásūnāṃ svásādityā́nām amṛ́tasya nā́bhiḥ
prá nú vocaṃ cikitúṣe jánāya mā́ gā́m ánāgām áditiṃ vadhiṣṭa
The Rudras' Mother, Daughter of the Vasus, centre of nectar, the Âdityas' Sister — To folk who understand will I proclaim it — injure not Aditi, the Cow, the sinless.
दे॒वीं दे॒वेभ्यः॒ पर्ये॒युषीं॒ गामा मा॑वृक्त॒ मर्त्यो॑ द॒भ्रचे॑ताः
vacovídaṃ vā́cam udīráyantīṃ víśvābhir dhībhír upatíṣṭhamānām
devī́ṃ devébhyaḥ páry eyúṣīṃ gā́m ā́ māvṛkta mártyo dabhrácetāḥ
Weak-minded men have as a cow adopted me who came hither from the Gods, a Goddess, Who, skilled in eloquence, her voice uplifteth, who standeth near at hand with all devotions.
102: tvám agne bṛhád váyo dádhāsi deva dāśúṣe
LORD of the house, Sage, ever young, high power of life, O Agni, God, Thou givest to thy worshipper.
स न॒ ईळा॑नया स॒ह दे॒वाँ अ॑ग्ने दुव॒स्युवा॑
sá na ī́ḷānayā sahá devā́m̐ agne duvasyúvā
So with our song that prays and serves, attentive, Lord of spreading light, Agni, bring hitherward the Gods.
त्वया॑ ह स्विद्यु॒जा व॒यं चोदि॑ष्ठेन यविष्ठ्य
tváyā ha svid yujā́ vayáṃ códiṣṭhena yaviṣṭhya
For, Ever-Youthful One, with thee, best Furtherer, as our ally, We overcome, to win the spoil.
As Aurva Bhrigu used, as Apnavâna used, I call the pure Agni who clothes him with the sea.
I call the Sage who sounds like wind, the Might that like Parjanya roars, Agni who clothes him with the sea.
आ स॒वं स॑वि॒तुर्य॑था॒ भग॑स्येव भु॒जिं हु॑वे
ā́ saváṃ savitúr yathā bhágasyeva bhujíṃ huve
As Savitar's productive Power, as him who sends down bliss, I call Agni who clothes him with the sea.
Hither, for powerful kirship, I call Agni, him Who prospers you, Most frequent at our solemn rites
अ॒यं यथा॑ न आ॒भुव॒त्त्वष्टा॑ रू॒पेव॒ तक्ष्या॑
ayáṃ yáthā na ābhúvat tváṣṭā rūpéva tákṣyā
That through this famed One's power, he may stand by us even as Tvashṭar comes Unto the forms that must be shaped.
ayáṃ víśvā abhí śríyo 'gnír devéṣu patyate
This Agni is the Lord supreme above all glories mid the Gods: May he come nigh to us with strength.
Here praise ye him the most renowned of all the ministering Priests, Agni, the Chief at sacrifice;
śīrám pāvakáśociṣaṃ jyéṣṭho yó dámeṣv ā́
Piercing, with purifying flame, enkindled in our homes, most high, Swiftest to hear from far away.
तमर्व॑न्तं॒ न सा॑न॒सिं गृ॑णी॒हि वि॑प्र शु॒ष्मिण॑म्
tám árvantaṃ ná sānasíṃ gṛṇīhí vipra śuṣmíṇam
Sage, laud the Mighty One who wins the spoil of victory like a steed, And, Mitra-like, unites the folk.
úpa tvā jāmáyo gíro dédiśatīr haviṣkṛ́taḥ
Still turning to their aim in thee, the oblation-bearer's sister hymns Have come to thee before the wind.
yásya tridhā́tv ávṛtam barhís tasthā́v ásaṃdinam
The waters find their place in him, for whom the threefold sacred grass Is spread unbound, unlimited.
The station of the Bounteous God hath, through his aid which none impair, A pleasant aspect like the Sun.
ágne ghṛtásya dhītíbhis tepānó deva śocíṣā
Blazing with splendour, Agni, God, through pious gifts of sacred oil, Bring thou the Gods and worship them.
तं त्वा॑जनन्त मा॒तरः॑ क॒विं दे॒वासो॑ अङ्गिरः
táṃ tvājananta mātáraḥ kavíṃ devā́so aṅgiraḥ
The Gods as mothers brought thee forth, the Immortal Sage, O Angiras, The bearer of our gifts to heaven.
Wise Agni, Gods established thee, the Seer, noblest messenger, As bearer of our sacred gifts.
nahí me ásty ághnyā ná svádhitir vánanvati
No cow have I to call mine own, no axe at hand wherewith to work, Yet what is here I bring to thee.
यद॑ग्ने॒ कानि॒ कानि॑ चि॒दा ते॒ दारू॑णि द॒ध्मसि॑
yád agne kā́ni kā́ni cid ā́ te dā́rūṇi dadhmási
O Agni, whatsoever be the fuel that we lay for thee, Be pleased therewith, Most Youthful God.
yád átty upajíhvikā yád vamró atisárpati
That which the white-ant eats away, that over which the emmet crawls — May all of this be oil to thee.
agním índhāno mánasā dhíyaṃ saceta mártyaḥ
When he enkindles Agni, man should with his heart attend the song: I with the priests have kindled him.
103: उपो॒ षु जा॒तमार्य॑स्य॒ वर्ध॑नम॒ग्निं न॑क्षन्त नो॒ गिरः॑
úpo ṣú jātám ā́ryasya várdhanam agníṃ nakṣanta no gíraḥ
THAT noblest Furtherer hath appeared, to whom men bring their holy works. Our songs of praise have risen aloft to Agni who was barn to give the Ârya strength.
प्र दैवो॑दासो अ॒ग्निर्दे॒वाँ अच्छा॒ न म॒ज्मना॑
अनु॑ मा॒तरं॑ पृथि॒वीं वि वा॑वृते त॒स्थौ नाक॑स्य॒ सान॑वि
prá daívodāso agnír devā́m̐ áchā ná majmánā
ánu mātáram pṛthivī́ṃ ví vāvṛte tasthaú nā́kasya sā́navi
Agni of Divodâsa turned, as 'twere in majesty, to the Gods. Onward he sped along the mother earth, and took his station in the height of heaven.
sahasrasā́m medhásātāv iva tmánāgníṃ dhībhíḥ saparyata
Him before whom the people shrink when he performs his glorious deeds, Him who wins thousands at the worship of the Gods, himself, that Agni, serve with son s.

prá yáṃ rāyé nínīṣasi márto yás te vaso dā́śat
sá vīráṃ dhatte agna ukthaśaṃsínaṃ tmánā sahasrapoṣíṇam
The mortal man whom thou wouldst lead to opulence, O Vasu, he who brings thee gifts. He, Agni, wins himself a hero singing lauds, yea, one who feeds a thousand men.
स दृ॒ळ्हे चि॑द॒भि तृ॑णत्ति॒ वाज॒मर्व॑ता॒ स ध॑त्ते॒ अक्षि॑ति॒ श्रवः॑
त्वे दे॑व॒त्रा सदा॑ पुरूवसो॒ विश्वा॑ वा॒मानि॑ धीमहि
sá dṛḷhé cid abhí tṛṇatti vā́jam árvatā sá dhatte ákṣiti śrávaḥ
tvé devatrā́ sádā purūvaso víśvā vāmā́ni dhīmahi
He with the steed wins spoil even in the fenced fort, and gains imperishable fame. In thee, O Lord of wealth, continually we lay all precious offerings to the Gods.
यो विश्वा॒ दय॑ते॒ वसु॒ होता॑ म॒न्द्रो जना॑नाम्
मधो॒र्न पात्रा॑ प्रथ॒मान्य॑स्मै॒ प्र स्तोमा॑ यन्त्य॒ग्नये॑
yó víśvā dáyate vásu hótā mandró jánānām
mádhor ná pā́trā prathamā́ny asmai prá stómā yanty agnáye
To him who dealeth out all wealth, who is the cheerful Priest of men, To him, like the first vessels filled with savoury juice, to Agni go the songs of praise.
अश्वं॒ न गी॒र्भी र॒थ्यं॑ सु॒दान॑वो मर्मृ॒ज्यन्ते॑ देव॒यवः॑
उ॒भे तो॒के तन॑ये दस्म विश्पते॒ पर्षि॒ राधो॑ म॒घोना॑म्
áśvaṃ ná gīrbhī́ rathyàṃ sudā́navo marmṛjyánte devayávaḥ
ubhé toké tánaye dasma viśpate párṣi rā́dho maghónām
Votaries, richly-gifted, deck him with their songs, even as the steed who draws the car. On both, Strong Lord of men! on child and grandson pour the bounties which our nobles give.
प्र मंहि॑ष्ठाय गायत ऋ॒ताव्ने॑ बृह॒ते शु॒क्रशो॑चिषे
prá máṃhiṣṭhāya gāyata ṛtā́vne bṛhaté śukráśociṣe
Sing forth to him, the Holy, most munificent, sublime with his refulgent glow, To Agni, ye Upastutas.
आ वं॑सते म॒घवा॑ वी॒रव॒द्यशः॒ समि॑द्धो द्यु॒म्न्याहु॑तः
ā́ vaṃsate maghávā vīrávad yáśaḥ sámiddho dyumny ā́hutaḥ
kuvín no asya sumatír návīyasy áchā vā́jebhir āgámat
Worshipped with gifts, enkindled, splendid, Maghavan shall win himself heroic fame. And will not his most newly shown benevolence come to us with abundant strength?
Priest, presser of the juice! praise now the dearest Guest of all our friends, Agni, the driver of the cars.
उदि॑ता॒ यो निदि॑ता॒ वेदि॑ता॒ वस्वा य॒ज्ञियो॑ व॒वर्त॑ति
दु॒ष्टरा॒ यस्य॑ प्रव॒णे नोर्मयो॑ धि॒या वाजं॒ सिषा॑सतः
úditā yó níditā véditā vásv ā́ yajñíyo vavártati
duṣṭárā yásya pravaṇé nórmáyo dhiyā́ vā́jaṃ síṣāsataḥ
Who, finder-out of treasures open and concealed, bringeth them hither, Holy One; Whose waves, as in a cataract, are hard to pass, when he, through song, would win him strength.
mā́ no hṛṇītām átithir vásur agníḥ purupraśastá eṣáḥ
Let not the noble Guest, Agni, be wroth with us: by many a man his praise is sung, Good Herald, skilled in sacrifice.
mó té riṣan yé áchoktibhir vasó 'gne kébhiś cid évaiḥ
kīríś cid dhí tvā́m ī́ṭṭe dūtyāā̀ya rātáhavyaḥ svadhvaráḥ
O Vasu, Agni, let not them be harmed who come in any way with lauds to thee. Even the lowly, skilled in rites, with offered gifts, seeketh thee for the envoy's task.
Friend of the Maruts, Agni, come with Rudras to the Soma-draught, To Sobharî's fair song of praise, and be thou joyful in the light.
